## Add-PWUsersToCloudProjectsByUserLists


NAME
    Add-PWUsersToCloudProjectsByUserLists
    
SYNOPSIS
    Adds users in userlists to Bentley Infrastructure Cloud Projects.
    
    
SYNTAX
    Add-PWUsersToCloudProjectsByUserLists [[-InputFolders] <ProjectWiseFolder[]>] [[-UserLists] <string[]>] [-Token] <string> [[-Filter] <string>] [[-CloudProjectId] <string>] [[-Roles] <string[]>] [<CommonParameters>]
    
    
DESCRIPTION
    Takes an array of folders and associates users in the passed user lists or in all the project's user lists with the associated Bentley Infrastructure Cloud project. Or takes a Bentley Infrastructure Cloud project id instead of an array of folders.
    

PARAMETERS
    -InputFolders <ProjectWiseFolder[]>
        Array of ProjectWise folders from pipeline. The work areas with Bentley Infrastructure Cloud projects will have users added.
        
        Required?                    false
        Position?                    0
        Default value                PWPS_DAB.CommonTypes+ProjectWiseFolder[]
        Accept pipeline input?       true (ByValue)
        Accept wildcard characters?  false
        
    -UserLists <string[]>
        Users Lists containing participants to add to the Bentley Infrastructure Cloud projects. You can only leave this blank if passing in work areas instead of a Bentley Infrastructure Cloud project ID. If left blank, all users in the project user lists will be added.
        
        Required?                    false
        Position?                    1
        Default value                
        Accept pipeline input?       false
        Accept wildcard characters?  false
        
    -Token <string>
        Authentication token. Required. Use Get-PWConnectionClientToken
        
        Required?                    true
        Position?                    6
        Default value                
        Accept pipeline input?       false
        Accept wildcard characters?  false
        
    -Filter <string>
        Optional string wildcard filter to select the resolved user lists. Originally indented for the case where input folders are passed in instead of the Bentley Infrastructure Cloud project id and no user lists are passed in..
        
        Required?                    false
        Position?                    7
        Default value                
        Accept pipeline input?       false
        Accept wildcard characters?  false
        
    -Roles <string[]>
        Array of roles.
        
        Required?                    false
        Position?                    8
        Default value                
        Accept pipeline input?       false
        Accept wildcard characters?  false
        
    -CloudProjectId <string>
        Pass Bentley Infrastructure Cloud Project Guid string if you have it instead of folders.
        
        Required?                    false
        Position?                    8
        Default value                
        Accept pipeline input?       false
        Accept wildcard characters?  false
        
    <CommonParameters>
        This cmdlet supports the common parameters: Verbose, Debug,
        ErrorAction, ErrorVariable, WarningAction, WarningVariable,
        OutBuffer, PipelineVariable, and OutVariable. For more information, see 
        about_CommonParameters (https:/go.microsoft.com/fwlink/?LinkID=113216). 
    
INPUTS
    PWPS_DAB.CommonTypes+ProjectWiseFolder[]
        Array of ProjectWise folders from pipeline. The work areas with Bentley Infrastructure Cloud projects will have users added.
    
    
OUTPUTS
    
    ----------  EXAMPLE 1  ----------
    
    #Example usage for adding users to a Bentley Infrastructure Cloud project.
    #Will add all the users in all the user lists to each associated Bentley Infrastructure Cloud Project in the entire datasource.
    New-PWLogin
    $CCToken = Get-PWConnectionClientToken
    Get-PWRichProjects | Add-PWUsersToCloudProjectsByUserLists -Token $CCToken
    
    ----------  EXAMPLE 2  ----------
    
    #Example will add all the users in the filtered user lists to the Bentley Infrastructure Cloud Projects.
    New-PWLogin
    $CCToken = Get-PWConnectionClientToken
    Get-PWFolders -FolderPath 'Projects\2020-05-19' | Add-PWUsersToCloudProjectsByUserLists -Filter "*Managers*" -Roles "Project Manager" -Token $CCToken
    
    ----------  EXAMPLE 3  ----------
    
    #Example will create a Bentley Infrastructure Cloud project and add users from userlist1 and userlist2.
    New-PWLogin
    $CCToken = Get-PWConnectionClientToken
    $OIDCToken = Get-OIDCToken -Authority "https://ims.bentley.com"
    $CloudProjectId = Add-CloudProject -CloudProjectName MyCloudProjectName -CloudProjectNumber MyCloudProjectNumber -OIDCToken $oidcToken
    Add-PWUsersToCloudProjectsByUserLists -CloudProjectId $CloudProjectId -UserLists userlist1,userlist2 -Roles Engineer -Token $CCToken
    
    
RELATED LINKS

## Add-PWUsersToConnectedProject


NAME
    Add-PWUsersToConnectedProject
    
SYNOPSIS
    Takes an array of user objects from the pipeline and associates them with the CONNECTed project associated with the rich project given a ProjectWise folder path.
    
    
SYNTAX
    Add-PWUsersToConnectedProject [[-InputUsers] <User[]>] [[-FolderPath] <string>] [[-ConnectedProjectUser] <string>] [[-ConnectedProjectPassword] <SecureString>] [[-Review] <SwitchParameter>] [[-Issue] <SwitchParameter>] [[-Receive] <SwitchParameter>] [[-Administrator] 
    <SwitchParameter>] [-Token] <string> [[-Roles] <string[]>] [[-ConnectedProjectId] <string>] [[-Emails] <string[]>] [<CommonParameters>]
    
    
DESCRIPTION
    Takes an array of user objects from the pipeline and associates them with the CONNECTed project associated with the rich project given a ProjectWise folder path. You can specify the rights each user should be given. Only users with email addresses specified will be added to the 
    CONNECTed project.
    

PARAMETERS
    -InputUsers <User[]>
        Array of ProjectWise User objects from the pipeline.
        
        Required?                    false
        Position?                    0
        Default value                
        Accept pipeline input?       true (ByValue)
        Accept wildcard characters?  false
        
    -FolderPath <string>
        Path to the rich project from which we'll find the associated CONNECTed project.
        
        Required?                    false
        Position?                    1
        Default value                
        Accept pipeline input?       false
        Accept wildcard characters?  false
        
    -Review <SwitchParameter>
        Set to grant Review privileges to the users.
        
        Required?                    false
        Position?                    2
        Default value                False
        Accept pipeline input?       false
        Accept wildcard characters?  false
        
    -Issue <SwitchParameter>
        Set to grant Issue privileges to the users.
        
        Required?                    false
        Position?                    3
        Default value                False
        Accept pipeline input?       false
        Accept wildcard characters?  false
        
    -Receive <SwitchParameter>
        Set to grant Receive privileges to the users.
        
        Required?                    false
        Position?                    4
        Default value                False
        Accept pipeline input?       false
        Accept wildcard characters?  false
        
    -Administrator <SwitchParameter>
        Set to grant Administrator privileges to the users.
        
        Required?                    false
        Position?                    5
        Default value                False
        Accept pipeline input?       false
        Accept wildcard characters?  false
        
    -ConnectedProjectUser <string>
        DEPRECATED -- use Token instead.
        
        Required?                    false
        Position?                    10
        Default value                
        Accept pipeline input?       false
        Accept wildcard characters?  false
        
    -ConnectedProjectPassword <SecureString>
        DEPRECATED -- use Token instead.
        
        Required?                    false
        Position?                    11
        Default value                
        Accept pipeline input?       false
        Accept wildcard characters?  false
        
    -Token <string>
        Pass token to use for connection.
        
        Required?                    true
        Position?                    6
        Default value                
        Accept pipeline input?       false
        Accept wildcard characters?  false
        
    -Roles <string[]>
        Array of roles.
        
        Required?                    false
        Position?                    7
        Default value                
        Accept pipeline input?       false
        Accept wildcard characters?  false
        
    -ConnectedProjectId <string>
        Pass Connected Project Guid string.
        
        Required?                    false
        Position?                    8
        Default value                
        Accept pipeline input?       false
        Accept wildcard characters?  false
        
    -Emails <string[]>
        Array of user emails (e.g. "user.one@companytwo.com","user.two@companythree.com").
        
        Required?                    false
        Position?                    9
        Default value                
        Accept pipeline input?       false
        Accept wildcard characters?  false
        
    <CommonParameters>
        This cmdlet supports the common parameters: Verbose, Debug,
        ErrorAction, ErrorVariable, WarningAction, WarningVariable,
        OutBuffer, PipelineVariable, and OutVariable. For more information, see 
        about_CommonParameters (https:/go.microsoft.com/fwlink/?LinkID=113216). 
    
INPUTS
    Bentley.ProjectWise.PowerShell.Common.User[]
        Array of ProjectWise User objects from the pipeline.
    
    
OUTPUTS
    
    ----------  EXAMPLE 1  ----------
    
    #Example usage for adding users to a CONNECTED project.
    #Will add the users with email who have logged in within the last year to the CONNECTed Project associated with the ProjectWise Rich Project identified by that path
    Get-PWUserByLastLogin -DaysAgo 365 -Since | Add-PWUsersToConnectedProject -FolderPath "PWPS Connected Project Test 6\Projects 2\Project A"
    
    ----------  EXAMPLE 2  ----------
    
    $bentleyToken = Get-PWConnectionClientToken
    $suffix = Get-RandomString -Length 5 -Characters 'ABCEDFGHIJKLMNOPQRSTUVWXYZ'
    $connProj = Add-PWConnectedProject -ConnectedProjectName "Golf Hotel Indigo $suffix" -ConnectedProjectNumber "Golf Hotel Indigo $suffix" -MakeUnique -Location 'Durham, NC' -AssetType 'Airport' -WSGURL 'https://decide-pwce-us-ws.bentley.com/ws' -Token $bentleyToken
    #wait a few seconds before querying for the roles. It takes a bit for them all to get populated
    $roles = Get-PWConnectedProjectRoles $connProj -Token $bentleyToken
    Add-PWUsersToConnectedProject -ConnectedProjectId $connProj -Token $bentleyToken -Emails "fred.jones@acme.com","john.smith@acme.com" -Roles $roles
    
    
RELATED LINKS

## Add-PWUsersToConnectedProject2


NAME
    Add-PWUsersToConnectedProject2

DESCRIPTION
    Adds users to a connected project. These users can be an array of user objects from the pipeline or a comma separated list of emails passed in with the Email parameter. The project itself can be specified by providing a work area path that has an associated connected project or the 
    GUID id.
    

PARAMETERS
    -InputUsers <User[]>
        Array of ProjectWise User objects from the pipeline.
        
        Required?                    false
        Position?                    0
        Default value                
        Accept pipeline input?       true (ByValue)
        Accept wildcard characters?  false
        
    -FolderPath <string>
        Path to the rich project from which we'll find the associated CONNECTed project.
        
        Required?                    false
        Position?                    1
        Default value                
        Accept pipeline input?       false
        Accept wildcard characters?  false
        
    -Token <string>
        Pass token to use for connection.
        
        Required?                    true
        Position?                    6
        Default value                
        Accept pipeline input?       false
        Accept wildcard characters?  false
        
    -Roles <string[]>
        Array of roles.
        
        Required?                    false
        Position?                    7
        Default value                
        Accept pipeline input?       false
        Accept wildcard characters?  false
        
    -ConnectedProjectId <string>
        Pass Connected Project Guid string.
        
        Required?                    false
        Position?                    8
        Default value                
        Accept pipeline input?       false
        Accept wildcard characters?  false
        
    -Emails <string[]>
        Array of user emails (e.g. "user.one@companytwo.com","user.two@companythree.com").
        
        Required?                    false
        Position?                    9
        Default value                
        Accept pipeline input?       false
        Accept wildcard characters?  false
        
    <CommonParameters>
        This cmdlet supports the common parameters: Verbose, Debug,
        ErrorAction, ErrorVariable, WarningAction, WarningVariable,
        OutBuffer, PipelineVariable, and OutVariable. For more information, see 
        about_CommonParameters (https:/go.microsoft.com/fwlink/?LinkID=113216). 
    
INPUTS
    Bentley.ProjectWise.PowerShell.Common.User[]
        Array of ProjectWise User objects from the pipeline.
    
    
OUTPUTS
    
    ----------  EXAMPLE 1  ----------
    
    #Example usage for adding users to a connected project.
    #Will add the users with email who have logged in within the last year to the CONNECTed Project associated with the ProjectWise Rich Project identified by that path
    Get-PWUserByLastLogin -DaysAgo 365 -Since | Add-PWUsersToConnectedProject2 -FolderPath "PWPS Connected Project Test 6\Projects 2\Project A"
    
    ----------  EXAMPLE 2  ----------

    $suffix = Get-RandomString -Length 5 -Characters 'ABCEDFGHIJKLMNOPQRSTUVWXYZ'
    $connProj = Add-PWConnectedProject2 -ConnectedProjectName "Golf Hotel Indigo $suffix" -ConnectedProjectNumber "Golf Hotel Indigo $suffix" -MakeUnique -Location 'Durham, NC' -AssetType 'Airport' -WSGURL 'https://your-gateway/ws' -Token $bentleyToken
    #wait a few seconds before querying for the roles. It takes a bit for them all to get populated
    $roles = Get-PWConnectedProjectRoles $connProj -Token $bentleyToken
    Add-PWUsersToConnectedProject2 -ConnectedProjectId $connProj -Token $bentleyToken -Emails "fred.jones@acme.com","john.smith@acme.com" -Roles $roles

## Add-PWUsersToPW365Project


NAME
    Add-PWUsersToPW365Project
    
SYNOPSIS
    Takes an array of user objects from the pipeline and associates them with the ProjectWise365 project associated with the WorkArea given a ProjectWise folder path.
    
    
SYNTAX
    Add-PWUsersToPW365Project [[-InputUsers] <User[]>] [[-FolderPath] <string>] [[-Review] <SwitchParameter>] [[-Issue] <SwitchParameter>] [[-Receive] <SwitchParameter>] [[-Administrator] <SwitchParameter>] [-Token] <string> [[-Roles] <string[]>] [[-PW365ProjectId] <string>] [[-Emails] 
    <string[]>] [<CommonParameters>]
    
    
DESCRIPTION
    Takes an array of user objects from the pipeline and associates them with the ProjectWise365 project associated with the WorkArea given a ProjectWise folder path. You can specify the rights each user should be given. Only users with email addresses specified will be added to the 
    ProjectWise365 project.
    

PARAMETERS
    -InputUsers <User[]>
        Array of ProjectWise User objects from the pipeline.
        
        Required?                    false
        Position?                    0
        Default value                
        Accept pipeline input?       true (ByValue)
        Accept wildcard characters?  false
        
    -FolderPath <string>
        Path to the rich project from which we'll find the associated ProjectWise 365 project.
        
        Required?                    false
        Position?                    1
        Default value                
        Accept pipeline input?       false
        Accept wildcard characters?  false
        
    -Review <SwitchParameter>
        Set to grant Review privileges to the users.
        
        Required?                    false
        Position?                    2
        Default value                False
        Accept pipeline input?       false
        Accept wildcard characters?  false
        
    -Issue <SwitchParameter>
        Set to grant Issue privileges to the users.
        
        Required?                    false
        Position?                    3
        Default value                False
        Accept pipeline input?       false
        Accept wildcard characters?  false
        
    -Receive <SwitchParameter>
        Set to grant Receive privileges to the users.
        
        Required?                    false
        Position?                    4
        Default value                False
        Accept pipeline input?       false
        Accept wildcard characters?  false
        
    -Administrator <SwitchParameter>
        Set to grant Administrator privileges to the users.
        
        Required?                    false
        Position?                    5
        Default value                False
        Accept pipeline input?       false
        Accept wildcard characters?  false
        
    -Token <string>
        Pass token to use for connection.
        
        Required?                    true
        Position?                    6
        Default value                
        Accept pipeline input?       false
        Accept wildcard characters?  false
        
    -Roles <string[]>
        Array of roles.
        
        Required?                    false
        Position?                    7
        Default value                
        Accept pipeline input?       false
        Accept wildcard characters?  false
        
    -PW365ProjectId <string>
        Pass ProjectWise 365 Project Guid string.
        
        Required?                    false
        Position?                    8
        Default value                
        Accept pipeline input?       false
        Accept wildcard characters?  false
        
    -Emails <string[]>
        Array of user emails (e.g. "user.one@companytwo.com","user.two@companythree.com").
        
        Required?                    false
        Position?                    9
        Default value                
        Accept pipeline input?       false
        Accept wildcard characters?  false
        
    <CommonParameters>
        This cmdlet supports the common parameters: Verbose, Debug,
        ErrorAction, ErrorVariable, WarningAction, WarningVariable,
        OutBuffer, PipelineVariable, and OutVariable. For more information, see 
        about_CommonParameters (https:/go.microsoft.com/fwlink/?LinkID=113216). 
    
INPUTS
    Bentley.ProjectWise.PowerShell.Common.User[]
        Array of ProjectWise User objects from the pipeline.
    
    
OUTPUTS
    
    ----------  EXAMPLE 1  ----------
    
    #Example usage for adding users to a ProjectWise365 project.
    #Will add the users with email who have logged in within the last year to the ProjectWise365 Project associated with the WorkArea identified by that path
    Get-PWUserByLastLogin -DaysAgo 365 -Since | Add-PWUsersToPW365Project -FolderPath "PWPS ProjectWise365 Project Test 6\Projects 2\Project A"
    
    ----------  EXAMPLE 2  ----------
    
    $bentleyToken = Get-PWConnectionClientToken
    $suffix = Get-RandomString -Length 5 -Characters 'ABCEDFGHIJKLMNOPQRSTUVWXYZ'
    $pw365Proj = Add-PW365Project -PW365ProjectName "Golf Hotel Indigo $suffix" -PW365ProjectNumber "Golf Hotel Indigo $suffix" -MakeUnique -Location 'Durham, NC' -AssetType 'Airport' -WSGURL 'https://YourWSGUrl/ws' -Token $bentleyToken
    #wait a few seconds before querying for the roles. It takes a bit for them all to get populated
    $roles = Get-PW365ProjectRoles $connProj -Token $bentleyToken
    Add-PWUsersToPW365Project -PW365ProjectId $connProj -Token $bentleyToken -Emails "fred.jones@acme.com","sam.smith@acme.com" -Roles $roles

## CheckIn-PWDocumentsOrFree


NAME
    CheckIn-PWDocumentsOrFree
    
SYNOPSIS
    Check in, free or Import exported documents passed in the pipeline.
    
    
SYNTAX
    CheckIn-PWDocumentsOrFree [-InputDocument] <ProjectWiseDocument[]> [-Free <SwitchParameter>] [-ImportFolder <string>] [<CommonParameters>]
    
    
DESCRIPTION
    Input array of ProjectWiseDocument objects from the pipeline (Required). Use Get-PWDocumentBySearch to feed pipeline. Include the -Free switch parameter to free the documents. The cmdlet will determine if a document is CheckedOut or Exported and either checkin or import the 
    document. If the local file is missing, the file will be freed regardless of whether or not the -Free switch parameter is included.
    

PARAMETERS
    -InputDocument <ProjectWiseDocument[]>
        
        Required?                    true
        Position?                    0
        Default value                
        Accept pipeline input?       true (ByValue)
        Accept wildcard characters?  false
        
    -Free <SwitchParameter>
        
        Required?                    false
        Position?                    named
        Default value                False
        Accept pipeline input?       false
        Accept wildcard characters?  false
        
    -ImportFolder <string>
        
        Required?                    false
        Position?                    named
        Default value                
        Accept pipeline input?       false
        Accept wildcard characters?  false
        
    <CommonParameters>
        This cmdlet supports the common parameters: Verbose, Debug,
        ErrorAction, ErrorVariable, WarningAction, WarningVariable,
        OutBuffer, PipelineVariable, and OutVariable. For more information, see 
        about_CommonParameters (https:/go.microsoft.com/fwlink/?LinkID=113216). 
    
INPUTS
    PWPS_DAB.CommonTypes+ProjectWiseDocument[]
    
    
OUTPUTS
    
    ----------  EXAMPLE 1  ----------
    
    #Example usage for checking in document(s).
    #Get the documents in the folder where filename like *.dgn and check them in.
    Get-PWDocumentsBySearch -FolderPath 'Microstation J' -FileName '%.dgn' | CheckIn-PWDocumentsOrFree | Select-Object FileName
    #Should check in all the checked out documents passed to the cmdlet
    
    ----------  EXAMPLE 2  ----------
    
    #Example usage for freeing a document(s).
    #Get the documents in the folder where filename like *.dgn and check them in.
    Get-PWDocumentsBySearch -FolderPath 'Microstation J' -FileName '%.dgn' | CheckIn-PWDocumentsOrFree -Free | Select-Object FileName
    #Should free all the checked out documents passed to the cmdlet

        Required?                    false
        Position?                    named
        Default value                
        Accept pipeline input?       false
        Accept wildcard characters?  false
        
    -NewUserName <string>
        Optional new user name to apply to user.
        
        Required?                    false
        Position?                    named

        Required?                    false
        Position?                    named
        Default value                False
        Accept pipeline input?       false
        Accept wildcard characters?  false
        
    -Emails <string[]>
        Array of user emails (e.g. "user.one@companytwo.com","user.two@companythree.com").
        
        Required?                    false
        Position?                    named
        Default value                
        Accept pipeline input?       false

OUTPUTS

## CopyOut-PWDocuments


NAME
    CopyOut-PWDocuments
    
SYNOPSIS
    Copies out documents. Note: If you want the cmdlet to behave closest to the way ProjectWise Explorer CopyOut does, use none of the available switches.
    
    
SYNTAX
    CopyOut-PWDocuments [-InputDocument] <ProjectWiseDocument[]> [[-NoReferences] <SwitchParameter>] [[-RemoveCopies] <SwitchParameter>] [<CommonParameters>]
    
    CopyOut-PWDocuments [-InputDocument] <ProjectWiseDocument[]> [[-Refresh] <SwitchParameter>] [[-OverwriteLocalCopy] <SwitchParameter>] [[-KeepUpToDateLocalCopy] <SwitchParameter>] [[-NoReferences] <SwitchParameter>] [[-RemoveCopies] <SwitchParameter>] [<CommonParameters>]
    
    
DESCRIPTION
    

PARAMETERS
    -InputDocument <ProjectWiseDocument[]>
        Input array of ProjectWiseDocument objects from the pipeline (Required). Use Get-PWDocumentBySearch or New-PWDocument to feed pipeline.
        
        Required?                    true
        Position?                    0
        Default value                
        Accept pipeline input?       true (ByValue)
        Accept wildcard characters?  false
        
    -Refresh <SwitchParameter>
        Use this switch to refresh of the local copy.
        
        Required?                    false
        Position?                    1
        Default value                False
        Accept pipeline input?       false
        Accept wildcard characters?  false
        
    -OverwriteLocalCopy <SwitchParameter>
        Use this switch to copy over local copy with copy from server regardless of local copy has been changed. It must be used with the NoReferences switch. It cannot be used with the KeepUpToDateLocalCopy switch.
        
        Required?                    false
        Position?                    2
        Default value                False
        Accept pipeline input?       false
        Accept wildcard characters?  false
        
    -KeepUpToDateLocalCopy <SwitchParameter>
        Use this switch to copy over an up to date file in the working directory. It must be used with the NoReferences switch. It cannot be used with the OverwriteLocalCopy switch.
        
        Required?                    false
        Position?                    3
        Default value                False
        Accept pipeline input?       false
        Accept wildcard characters?  false
        
    -NoReferences <SwitchParameter>
        Use this switch to skip the references on a copy out.
        
        Required?                    false
        Position?                    4
        Default value                False
        Accept pipeline input?       false
        Accept wildcard characters?  false
        
    -RemoveCopies <SwitchParameter>
        Use this switch in the fetch-files scenario where it is unnecessary to keep the documents in the working folder. The copy out should have handled getting the files cached on the caching server. No need to double the storage requirements.
        
        Required?                    false
        Position?                    5
        Default value                False
        Accept pipeline input?       false
        Accept wildcard characters?  false
        
    <CommonParameters>
        This cmdlet supports the common parameters: Verbose, Debug,
        ErrorAction, ErrorVariable, WarningAction, WarningVariable,
        OutBuffer, PipelineVariable, and OutVariable. For more information, see 
        about_CommonParameters (https:/go.microsoft.com/fwlink/?LinkID=113216). 
    
INPUTS
    PWPS_DAB.CommonTypes+ProjectWiseDocument[]
        Input array of ProjectWiseDocument objects from the pipeline (Required). Use Get-PWDocumentBySearch or New-PWDocument to feed pipeline.
    
    
OUTPUTS
    
    ----------  EXAMPLE 1  ----------

    #Gets the documents in this folder and subfolders where the file name pattern matches %.dwg
    $docs = Get-PWDocumentsBySearch -FolderPath 'BSI900 - Adelaide Tower\' -FileName '%.dwg'
    #Copies out all the found DWGs 
    $docs | CopyOut-PWDocuments

## Copy-PWDocumentsToFolder


NAME
    Copy-PWDocumentsToFolder

    Copies documents to a target folder.
    
    
SYNTAX
    Copy-PWDocumentsToFolder [-InputDocument] <ProjectWiseDocument[]> [-TargetFolderPath] <string> [[-CreateVersion] <SwitchParameter>] [[-IncludeVersions] <SwitchParameter>] [[-CopyReferenceRelationships] <SwitchParameter>] [<CommonParameters>]
    
    
DESCRIPTION
    Takes an array of document objects from the pipeline and copies them to a target folder.
    

PARAMETERS
    -InputDocument <ProjectWiseDocument[]>
        Array of document objects from pipeline (Required).
        
        Required?                    true
        Position?                    0
        Default value                
        Accept pipeline input?       true (ByValue)
        Accept wildcard characters?  false
        
    -TargetFolderPath <string>
        Path to target folder (Required).
        
        Required?                    true
        Position?                    1
        Default value                
        Accept pipeline input?       false
        Accept wildcard characters?  false
        
    -CreateVersion <SwitchParameter>
        Set this to create a new version if the document exists. If not set, document will be overwritten.
        
        Required?                    false
        Position?                    2
        Default value                False
        Accept pipeline input?       false
        Accept wildcard characters?  false
        
    -IncludeVersions <SwitchParameter>
        Set this to include document versions with the copy process. If not set, document versions will not be copied.
        
        Required?                    false
        Position?                    3
        Default value                False
        Accept pipeline input?       false
        Accept wildcard characters?  false
        
    -CopyReferenceRelationships <SwitchParameter>
        Set this to copy the reference relations.
        
        Required?                    false
        Position?                    4
        Default value                False
        Accept pipeline input?       false
        Accept wildcard characters?  false
        
    <CommonParameters>
        This cmdlet supports the common parameters: Verbose, Debug,
        ErrorAction, ErrorVariable, WarningAction, WarningVariable,
        OutBuffer, PipelineVariable, and OutVariable. For more information, see 
        about_CommonParameters (https:/go.microsoft.com/fwlink/?LinkID=113216).

    PWPS_DAB.CommonTypes+ProjectWiseDocument[]
        Array of document objects from pipeline (Required).
    
    
OUTPUTS
    
    ----------  EXAMPLE 1  ----------

    Get-PWDocumentsBySearch -FolderPath 'Import\Test' -FileName '02_%.pdf'| 
    Copy-PWDocumentsToFolder -TargetFolderPath 'New\Folder\Path' -Verbose
    
    ----------  EXAMPLE 2  ----------

    Copy-PWDocumentsToFolder -TargetFolderPath 'New\Folder\Path' -CreateVersion -Verbose
    
    ----------  EXAMPLE 3  ----------

    Get-PWDocumentsBySearch -FolderPath 'Import\Test' -FileName '02_%.pdf'| 
    Copy-PWDocumentsToFolder -TargetFolderPath 'New\Folder\Path' -IncludeVersions -Verbose

## Copy-PWFolder


NAME

    Copy-PWFolder copies a folder to the root directory or a specified target folder.

    Copy-PWFolder [-FolderPath] <string> [-FolderToCopy] <string> [-DontCopyWorkflow <SwitchParameter>] [-IncludeAccessControl <SwitchParameter>] [-IncludeDocuments <SwitchParameter>] [-IncludeSubFolders <SwitchParameter>] [-IncludeWorkspaceProfile <SwitchParameter>] 
    [-SkipFolderWorkflowSecurityReplication <SwitchParameter>] [-TargetPrefix <string>] [-TemplatePrefix <string>] [<CommonParameters>]
    
    Copy-PWFolder [-CreateAtRoot] <SwitchParameter> [-FolderToCopy] <string> [-DontCopyWorkflow <SwitchParameter>] [-IncludeAccessControl <SwitchParameter>] [-IncludeDocuments <SwitchParameter>] [-IncludeSubFolders <SwitchParameter>] [-IncludeWorkspaceProfile <SwitchParameter>] 
    [-SkipFolderWorkflowSecurityReplication <SwitchParameter>] [-TargetPrefix <string>] [-TemplatePrefix <string>] [<CommonParameters>]
    
    
DESCRIPTION
    Copy an existing folder into the root directory or another folder. Can include subfolders and/or documents, as well as document attributes, access control, workflow and workspace settings.
    

PARAMETERS
    -FolderPath <string>
        Full folder path of parent target folder. Required. Folder must exist.
        
        Required?                    true
        Position?                    0

        Accept pipeline input?       false

    -FolderToCopy <string>
        Path Name of folder to be copied. Required. Folder must exist.
        
        Required?                    true
        Position?                    2
        Default value                
        Accept pipeline input?       false
        Accept wildcard characters?  false
        
    -IncludeSubFolders <SwitchParameter>
        If included, all sub-folders will be copied.
        
        Required?                    false
        Position?                    named
        Default value                False
        Accept pipeline input?       false
        Accept wildcard characters?  false
        
    -DontCopyWorkflow <SwitchParameter>
        If included, the workflow setting will not be copied. By default, it will.
        
        Required?                    false
        Position?                    named
        Default value                False
        Accept pipeline input?       false
        Accept wildcard characters?  false
        
    -IncludeDocuments <SwitchParameter>
        If included, all documents will be copied.
        
        Required?                    false
        Position?                    named
        Default value                False
        Accept pipeline input?       false
        Accept wildcard characters?  false
        
    -IncludeAccessControl <SwitchParameter>
        If included, all access control will be copied.
        
        Required?                    false
        Position?                    named
        Default value                False
        Accept pipeline input?       false
        Accept wildcard characters?  false
        
    -IncludeWorkspaceProfile <SwitchParameter>
        If included, the workspace profile will be copied.
        
        Required?                    false
        Position?                    named
        Default value                False
        Accept pipeline input?       false
        Accept wildcard characters?  false
        
    -TemplatePrefix <string>
        Defaults to '[TEMPLATE]'. If TargetPrefix is set, will process user lists with that prefix into ones with the tempalte prefix ([TEMPLATE]_ProjectManagers => TargetPrefix_ProjectManagers)
        
        Required?                    false
        Position?                    named
        Default value                [TEMPLATE]
        Accept pipeline input?       false
        Accept wildcard characters?  false
        
    -TargetPrefix <string>
        If TargetPrefix is set, will process user lists with that prefix into ones with the template prefix ([TEMPLATE]_ProjectManagers => TargetPrefix_ProjectManagers)
        
        Required?                    false
        Position?                    named
        Default value                
        Accept pipeline input?       false
        Accept wildcard characters?  false
        
    -SkipFolderWorkflowSecurityReplication <SwitchParameter>
        Skip the Folder + Workflow security replication which can be quite time consuming. Workflow security whould probably be set globally anyway...
        
        Required?                    false
        Position?                    named
        Default value                False
        Accept pipeline input?       false
        Accept wildcard characters?  false

OUTPUTS

    This copies the dwgs folder into the projects folder. No documents or sub-folders are included.
    Copy-PWFolder -FolderPath "Projects" -FolderToCopy 'DWGS'
    
    ----------  EXAMPLE 2  ----------
    
    This copies the DWGS folder into the Project01 folder. Sub-folders and documents will be copied.
    Copy-PWFolder -FolderPath "Project Folder\Project 01" -FolderToCopy 'Working Folder\DWGS' -IncludeSubFolders -IncludeDocuments
    
    ----------  EXAMPLE 3  ----------

## Copy-PWSavedSearch


NAME
    Copy-PWSavedSearch
    
SYNOPSIS
    Copy a saved search to the datasource or to a Work Area.
    
    
SYNTAX
    Copy-PWSavedSearch [-SavedSearch] <string> [[-FolderPath] <string>] [[-FolderPath_Target] <string>] [-Personal <SwitchParameter>] [<CommonParameters>]
    
    Copy-PWSavedSearch [-SavedSearch] <string> [[-FolderID] <int>] [[-FolderPath_Target] <string>] [-Personal <SwitchParameter>] [<CommonParameters>]
    
    
DESCRIPTION
    Copy a saved search to the datasource or to a Work Area. Defaults to global saved search unless a target folder is included.
    

PARAMETERS
    -SavedSearch <string>
        Name of saved search to copy.
        
        Required?                    true
        Position?                    0
        Default value                
        Accept pipeline input?       false
        Accept wildcard characters?  false
        
    -FolderPath <string>
        Folder path of Work Area to search for saved searches.
        
        Required?                    false
        Position?                    1
        Default value                
        Accept pipeline input?       false
        Accept wildcard characters?  false
        
    -FolderID <int>
        Folder ID of Work Area to search for saved searches.
        
        Required?                    false
        Position?                    1
        Default value                0
        Accept pipeline input?       false
        Accept wildcard characters?  false
        
    -FolderPath_Target <string>
        Folder path to copy saved search to.
        
        Required?                    false
        Position?                    2
        Default value                
        Accept pipeline input?       false
        Accept wildcard characters?  false
        
    -Personal <SwitchParameter>
        Set this to copy the current user's saved search.
        
        Required?                    false
        Position?                    named
        Default value                False
        Accept pipeline input?       false
        Accept wildcard characters?  false
        
    <CommonParameters>
        This cmdlet supports the common parameters: Verbose, Debug,
        ErrorAction, ErrorVariable, WarningAction, WarningVariable,
        OutBuffer, PipelineVariable, and OutVariable. For more information, see 
        about_CommonParameters (https:/go.microsoft.com/fwlink/?LinkID=113216). 
    
INPUTS
    
OUTPUTS
    
    ----------  EXAMPLE 1  ----------
    
    #Copies the 'TEST' saved search from  Work Area (specified by FolderID 177) to the Personal saved searches in Work Area 'BSI200 - Peterborough Geospatial Investigation'.
    Copy-PWSavedSearches -SavedSearch 'TEST' -FolderID 177 -FolderPath_Target 'BSI200 - Peterborough Geospatial Investigation' -Personal -Verbose
    
    ----------  EXAMPLE 2  ----------
    
    #Copies the 'AllDocs' saved search from Work Area 'BSI900 - Adelaide Tower' to the Global saved searches in Work Area 'BSI200 - Peterborough Geospatial Investigation'.
    Copy-PWSavedSearches -SavedSearch 'AllDocs' -FolderPath 'BSI900 - Adelaide Tower' -FolderPath_Target 'BSI200 - Peterborough Geospatial Investigation' -Verbose
    
    ----------  EXAMPLE 3  ----------
    
    #Copies the 'TEST' saved search from  Work Area (specified by FolderID 177) to the Personal saved searches at the database level.
    Copy-PWSavedSearches -SavedSearch 'TEST' -FolderID 177 -Personal -Verbose
    
    ----------  EXAMPLE 4  ----------
    
    #Copies the 'AllDocs' saved search from Work Area 'BSI900 - Adelaide Tower' to the Global saved searches at the datasource level.
    Copy-PWSavedSearches -SavedSearch 'AllDocs' -FolderPath 'BSI900 - Adelaide Tower' -Verbose

## Copy-PWSavedSearch2


NAME
    Copy-PWSavedSearch2
    
SYNOPSIS
    Copy a saved search to the datasource or to a Work Area.
    
    
SYNTAX
    Copy-PWSavedSearch2 [[-FromGlobalSearch] <string>] [[-FromPersonalSearch] <string>] [[-FromWorkAreaFolderID] <int>] [[-FromWorkAreaPath] <string>] [[-ToWorkAreaPath] <string>] [[-FromUserName] <string>] [[-ToUserName] <string>] [-FromDatasourceLevel <SwitchParameter>] 
    [-ToDatasourceLevel <SwitchParameter>] [-ToGlobalSearch <SwitchParameter>] [-ToPersonalSearch <SwitchParameter>] [<CommonParameters>]
    
    
DESCRIPTION
    Copy a saved search to the datasource or to a Work Area. Can copy between work areas, between datasource level and work areas and between global and personal searches. Note that the personal searches are that of the currently logged in user.
    

PARAMETERS
    -FromPersonalSearch <string>
        Name of saved search to copy. Search is personal.
        
        Required?                    false
        Position?                    0
        Default value                
        Accept pipeline input?       false
        Accept wildcard characters?  false
        
    -FromGlobalSearch <string>
        Name of saved search to copy. Search is global.
        
        Required?                    false
        Position?                    0
        Default value                
        Accept pipeline input?       false
        Accept wildcard characters?  false
        
    -FromWorkAreaPath <string>
        Folder path of Work Area to search for saved searches.
        
        Required?                    false
        Position?                    1
        Default value                
        Accept pipeline input?       false
        Accept wildcard characters?  false
        
    -FromWorkAreaFolderID <int>
        Folder ID of Work Area to search for saved searches.
        
        Required?                    false
        Position?                    1
        Default value                0
        Accept pipeline input?       false
        Accept wildcard characters?  false
        
    -ToWorkAreaPath <string>
        Work area path to copy saved search to.
        
        Required?                    false
        Position?                    2
        Default value                
        Accept pipeline input?       false
        Accept wildcard characters?  false
        
    -FromUserName <string>
        The name of user that owns the personal searches you wish to copy.
        
        Required?                    false
        Position?                    3
        Default value                
        Accept pipeline input?       false
        Accept wildcard characters?  false
        
    -ToUserName <string>
        The name of user that will own the personal searches you copy to.
        
        Required?                    false
        Position?                    4
        Default value                
        Accept pipeline input?       false
        Accept wildcard characters?  false
        
    -ToPersonalSearch <SwitchParameter>
        Set this to copy the search to the current user's saved search.
        
        Required?                    false
        Position?                    named
        Default value                False
        Accept pipeline input?       false
        Accept wildcard characters?  false
        
    -ToGlobalSearch <SwitchParameter>
        Set this to copy the search saved search.
        
        Required?                    false
        Position?                    named
        Default value                False
        Accept pipeline input?       false
        Accept wildcard characters?  false
        
    -FromDatasourceLevel <SwitchParameter>
        Set this to copy the search from the datasource level of the datasource.
        
        Required?                    false
        Position?                    named
        Default value                False
        Accept pipeline input?       false
        Accept wildcard characters?  false
        
    -ToDatasourceLevel <SwitchParameter>
        Set this to copy the search to the datasource level of the datasource.
        
        Required?                    false
        Position?                    named
        Default value                False
        Accept pipeline input?       false
        Accept wildcard characters?  false
        
    <CommonParameters>
        This cmdlet supports the common parameters: Verbose, Debug,
        ErrorAction, ErrorVariable, WarningAction, WarningVariable,
        OutBuffer, PipelineVariable, and OutVariable. For more information, see 
        about_CommonParameters (https:/go.microsoft.com/fwlink/?LinkID=113216). 
    
INPUTS
    
OUTPUTS
    
    ----------  EXAMPLE 1  ----------
    
    #Copies the 'TEST' personal saved search from  Work Area (specified by FromWorkAreaFolderID 177) to the Personal saved searches in Work Area 'BSI200 - Peterborough Geospatial Investigation'.
    Copy-PWSavedSearch2 -FromPersonalSearch 'TEST' -FromWorkAreaFolderID 177 -ToPersonalSearch -ToWorkAreaPath 'BSI200 - Peterborough Geospatial Investigation' -Personal -Verbose
    
    ----------  EXAMPLE 2  ----------
    
    #Copies the 'TEST' personal saved search from  Work Area 'BSI900 - Adelaide Tower' to the Personal saved searches in Work Area 'BSI200 - Peterborough Geospatial Investigation'.  The owner of the search to copy is 'user2'.  The owner of the search copy produced is 'user3.
    Copy-PWSavedSearch2 -FromPersonalSearch 'TEST' -FromWorkAreaPath 'BSI900 - Adelaide Tower' -ToPersonalSearch -ToWorkAreaPath 'BSI200 - Peterborough Geospatial Investigation' -Personal -FromUserName 'user2' -ToUserName 'user3' -Verbose
    
    ----------  EXAMPLE 3  ----------
    
    #Copies the 'AllDocs' global saved search from Work Area 'BSI900 - Adelaide Tower' to the Global saved searches in Work Area 'BSI200 - Peterborough Geospatial Investigation'.
    Copy-PWSavedSearch2 -FromGlobalSearch 'AllDocs' -FromWorkAreaPath 'BSI900 - Adelaide Tower' -ToGlobalSearch -ToWorkAreaPath 'BSI200 - Peterborough Geospatial Investigation' -Verbose
    
    ----------  EXAMPLE 4  ----------
    
    #Copies the 'TEST' global saved search from  Work Area (specified by FromWorkAreaFolderID 177) to the Personal saved searches at the database level.
    Copy-PWSavedSearch2 -FromGlobalSearch 'TEST' -FromWorkAreaFolderID 177 -ToPersonalSearch -ToDatasourceLevel -Verbose
    
    ----------  EXAMPLE 5  ----------
    
    #Copies the 'AllDocs' global saved search from Work Area 'BSI900 - Adelaide Tower' to the Global saved searches at the datasource level.
    Copy-PWSavedSearch2 -FromGlobalSearch 'AllDocs' -FromWorkAreaPath 'BSI900 - Adelaide Tower'  -ToGlobalSearch -ToDatasourceLevel -Verbose
    
    
RELATED LINKS

PARAMETERS
    -SourceDataTable <DataTable>
        
        Required?                    true
        Position?                    0
        Default value                
        Accept pipeline input?       false
        Accept wildcard characters?  false
        
    -OutputFolder <string>
        Folder on disk for output.
        
        Required?                    true
        Position?                    1
        Default value                
        Accept pipeline input?       false
        Accept wildcard characters?  false
        
    -OutputFileName <string>
        Optional output file name to use. Will use default name if not set.
        
        Required?                    false
        Position?                    2
        Default value                
        Accept pipeline input?       false
        Accept wildcard characters?  false
        
    -Append <SwitchParameter>
        When included, the SQLite Database will be appended if it exists.
        
        Required?                    false
        Position?                    named
        Default value                False
        Accept pipeline input?       false
        Accept wildcard characters?  false
        
    -Overwrite <SwitchParameter>
        When included, the SQLite Database will be replaced/overwritten if it exists.
        
        Required?                    false
        Position?                    named
        Default value                False
        Accept pipeline input?       false
        Accept wildcard characters?  false
        
    <CommonParameters>

    ----------  EXAMPLE 1  ----------
    
    Exports the SourceDataTable to a SQLite Database in the location specified.
    #SQLiteStudio seems like an adequate managment tool (http://sqlitestudio.pl/?act=download) for the resulting container.
    $dt = Get-PWDocumentReportDataTable -ProjectWiseFolder 'Design Drafting Projects\Test for Alignment Project' -Recurse
    $dt2 = $dt[0].Copy()
    Export-DataTableToSQLiteDB -SourceDataTable $dt2 -OutputFolder 'c:\temp'
    
    ----------  EXAMPLE 2  ----------
    
    Appends the SourceDataTable to a SQLite Database in the location specified.
    $dt = Get-PWDocumentReportDataTable -ProjectWiseFolder 'Design Drafting Projects\Test for Alignment Project' -Recurse
    $dt2 = $dt[0].Copy()
    Export-DataTableToSQLiteDB -SourceDataTable $dt2 -OutputFolder 'c:\temp' -Append
    
    ----------  EXAMPLE 3  ----------
    
    Overwrites (replaces) the existing SQLite Database. Exports the SourceDataTable to a SQLite Database in the location specified.
    $dt = Get-PWDocumentReportDataTable -ProjectWiseFolder 'Design Drafting Projects\Test for Alignment Project' -Recurse
    $dt2 = $dt[0].Copy()
    Export-DataTableToSQLiteDB -SourceDataTable $dt2 -OutputFolder 'c:\temp' -Overwrite

## Export-PWDocuments


NAME
    Export-PWDocuments
    
SYNOPSIS
    Despite the name, copies out files to a folder and optionally writes metadata to a spreadsheet.
    
    
SYNTAX
    Export-PWDocuments [[-InputDocuments] <ProjectWiseDocument[]>] [-OutputFolder] <string> [[-Personal] <SwitchParameter>] [[-UseDMSFolders] <SwitchParameter>] [[-UseUnderscores] <SwitchParameter>] [[-AltMetadataExportMethod] <SwitchParameter>] [[-ProjectWiseFolder] <string>] 
    [[-Searches] <string>] [[-ExportMetadata] <SwitchParameter>] [[-ExportMetadataFile] <string>] [[-ExportVersions] <SwitchParameter>] [[-JustOneFolder] <SwitchParameter>] [[-BPRCFile] <string>] [[-ServerIsUTC] <SwitchParameter>] [<CommonParameters>]
    
    
DESCRIPTION
    Export metadata files is in same format as Save-PWDocumentReport. NOTE: Version support assumes Document Name consistency in the version stack. The export will probably work, but the import from the spreadsheet assumes that document names are constant through the stack.
    
    Folder structure is preserved (even long paths so make sure you have a Windows File Explorer replacement that can navigate long paths).
    
    This will not overwrite a file on the disk unless the file in ProjectWise is newer. Intent is to maintain an up-to-date mirror of the files from ProjectWise on-disk. So, this cmdlet would be good for use in a scheduled task. Some users use this as a fetch-files replacement.
    
    The last file update date from ProjectWise and the ProjectWise document create date are preserved in the copied out file.
    

PARAMETERS
    -InputDocuments <ProjectWiseDocument[]>
        Input array of ProjectWiseDocument objects from the pipeline (Required). Use Get-PWDocumentBySearch or New-PWDocument to feed pipeline.
        
        Required?                    false
        Position?                    0
        Default value                
        Accept pipeline input?       true (ByValue)
        Accept wildcard characters?  false
        
    -OutputFolder <string>
        Folder on disk for output.
        
        Required?                    true
        Position?                    1
        Default value                
        Accept pipeline input?       false
        Accept wildcard characters?  false
        
    -ProjectWiseFolder <string>
        Optional ProjectWise folder path.
        
        Required?                    false
        Position?                    2
        Default value                
        Accept pipeline input?       false
        Accept wildcard characters?  false
        
    -Searches <string>
        Optional semi-colon delimited list of saved searches to process.
        
        Required?                    false
        Position?                    3
        Default value                
        Accept pipeline input?       false
        Accept wildcard characters?  false
        
    -ExportMetadata <SwitchParameter>
        Export metadata if set.
        
        Required?                    false
        Position?                    4
        Default value                False
        Accept pipeline input?       false
        Accept wildcard characters?  false
        
    -ExportMetadataFile <string>
        Metadata file name to use. Will use default name if not set.
        
        Required?                    false
        Position?                    5
        Default value                
        Accept pipeline input?       false
        Accept wildcard characters?  false
        
    -ExportVersions <SwitchParameter>
        If set, exports versions of files. Appends .verXXXX suffix before extension. Should always be used with ExportMetadata
        
        Required?                    false
        Position?                    6
        Default value                False
        Accept pipeline input?       false
        Accept wildcard characters?  false
        
    -JustOneFolder <SwitchParameter>
        If set, exports only the files in the given folder rather than including subfolders.
        
        Required?                    false
        Position?                    7
        Default value                False
        Accept pipeline input?       false
        Accept wildcard characters?  false
        
    -BPRCFile <string>
        If included, will build MicroStation batch processing file.
        
        Required?                    false
        Position?                    8
        Default value                
        Accept pipeline input?       false
        Accept wildcard characters?  false
        
    -ServerIsUTC <SwitchParameter>
        Set if server is UTC. Will do file time comparison in UTC.
        
        Required?                    false
        Position?                    9
        Default value                False
        Accept pipeline input?       false
        Accept wildcard characters?  false
        
    -Personal <SwitchParameter>
        Set to find personal search.
        
        Required?                    false
        Position?                    10
        Default value                False
        Accept pipeline input?       false

DESCRIPTION

        Position?                    0

        Accept pipeline input?       true (ByValue)
        Accept wildcard characters?  false
        
    -TargetFolder <string>

        Required?                    true
        Position?                    1
        Default value                
        Accept pipeline input?       false
        Accept wildcard characters?  false
        
    -ExportManagedDocs <SwitchParameter>
        Use to export managed copies of documents.
        
        Required?                    false
        Position?                    2
        Default value                False
        Accept pipeline input?       false
        Accept wildcard characters?  false
        
    <CommonParameters>

    [[-Overwrite] <SwitchParameter>] [<CommonParameters>]
    
    
DESCRIPTION

## Export-PWDocumentsToDataSet


NAME
    Export-PWDocumentsToDataSet
    
SYNOPSIS
    Report general data, metadata, and audit trail data to DataSet object. Should be usable with SQL Bulk Import.
    
    
SYNTAX
    Export-PWDocumentsToDataSet [[-ProjectWiseFolder] <string>] [[-SearchName] <string>] [[-OutputFile] <string>] [[-Personal] <SwitchParameter>] [[-NoAuditTrail] <SwitchParameter>] [[-ExcludeSecondaryAuditTrail] <SwitchParameter>] [<CommonParameters>]
    
    
DESCRIPTION
    #Will report on the documents returned by the saved search to an DataSet.
    
    Export-PWDocumentsToDataSet -SearchName "60% Complete"
    
    #Will report on documents in given folder to a DataSet.
    
    Export-PWDocumentsToDataSet -ProjectWiseFolder "Source A\Subfolder 1"
    

PARAMETERS
    -ProjectWiseFolder <string>
        Optional ProjectWise folder path.
        
        Required?                    false
        Position?                    0
        Default value                
        Accept pipeline input?       false
        Accept wildcard characters?  false
        
    -SearchName <string>
        Optional saved search name to process.
        
        Required?                    false
        Position?                    1
        Default value                
        Accept pipeline input?       false
        Accept wildcard characters?  false
        
    -OutputFile <string>
        SQLite output filename.
        
        Required?                    false
        Position?                    2
        Default value                
        Accept pipeline input?       false
        Accept wildcard characters?  false
        
    -Personal <SwitchParameter>
        Is personal search.
        
        Required?                    false
        Position?                    3
        Default value                False
        Accept pipeline input?       false
        Accept wildcard characters?  false
        
    -NoAuditTrail <SwitchParameter>
        Don't include audit trail.
        
        Required?                    false
        Position?                    4
        Default value                False
        Accept pipeline input?       false
        Accept wildcard characters?  false
        
    -ExcludeSecondaryAuditTrail <SwitchParameter>
        Don't include secondary audit trail records. Sometimes required for performance.
        
        Required?                    false
        Position?                    5
        Default value                False
        Accept pipeline input?       false
        Accept wildcard characters?  false
        
    <CommonParameters>
        This cmdlet supports the common parameters: Verbose, Debug,
        ErrorAction, ErrorVariable, WarningAction, WarningVariable,
        OutBuffer, PipelineVariable, and OutVariable. For more information, see 
        about_CommonParameters (https:/go.microsoft.com/fwlink/?LinkID=113216). 
    
INPUTS
    
OUTPUTS
    System.Data.DataSet
    
    
    ----------  EXAMPLE 1  ----------
    
    #Will report on the documents returned by the saved search to an DataSet.
    Export-PWDocumentsToDataSet -SearchName "60% Complete"
    #Will report on documents in given folder treee to a DataSet.
    Export-PWDocumentsToDataSet -ProjectWiseFolder "Source A\Subfolder 1"
    #DataSet output handling in PowerShell
    $ds=Export-PWDocumentsToDataSet -ProjectWiseFolder "Add Test Docs 01"
    foreach ($table in $ds.Tables)
    {
        Write-Host "TableName: $($table.TableName)"
        foreach ($column in $table.Columns)
        {
            write-Host "ColumnName: $($column.ColumnName), ColumnType: $($column.DataType)"
        }
        foreach ($row in $table.Rows)
        {
            foreach ($column in $table.Columns)
            {
                write-Host "$($column.ColumnName): $($row[$($column.ColumnName)])"
            }
        }
    }
    #Bulk copy into SQL Server. NB: used the OutputFile argument to save a SQLite copy of the data and then used the SQLite DDL to build a SQL Server table. Direct cut and paste.
    $ds=Export-PWDocumentsToDataSet -ProjectWiseFolder "Add Test Docs 01"
    $cn = new-object System.Data.SqlClient.SqlConnection("Data Source=brumd09515rem;User ID=sa;Password=pwd;Initial Catalog=BulkCopyTest");
    $cn.Open()    
    $bc = new-object ("System.Data.SqlClient.SqlBulkCopy") $cn
    $bc.DestinationTableName = "dbo.General_Documents_Table"
    $dtable=$ds.Tables["General_Documents_Table"]
    $bc.WriteToServer($dtable)
    $cn.Close()
    
    
RELATED LINKS

## Export-PWProjectAccessControl


NAME
    Export-PWProjectAccessControl
    
SYNOPSIS
    Export-PWProjectAccessControl is used to export out access control for a project/folder/work area to a datatable, Excel spreadsheet or SQLite database.
    
    
SYNTAX
    Export-PWProjectAccessControl [-InputFolder] <ProjectWiseFolder> [[-FolderLevel] <int>] [[-ExportFilePathName] <string>] [<CommonParameters>]
    
    Export-PWProjectAccessControl [-FolderPath] <string> [[-FolderLevel] <int>] [[-ExportFilePathName] <string>] [<CommonParameters>]
    
    Export-PWProjectAccessControl [-FolderID] <int> [[-FolderLevel] <int>] [[-ExportFilePathName] <string>] [<CommonParameters>]
    
    
DESCRIPTION
    Exports out access control from a folder(s) to a datatable by default. Exports to an Excel spreadsheet or SQLite database based on the value passed in the ExportFilePathName parameter.
    

PARAMETERS
    -InputFolder <ProjectWiseFolder>
        Source folder object(s) from pipeline.
        
        Required?                    true
        Position?                    0
        Default value                
        Accept pipeline input?       true (ByValue)
        Accept wildcard characters?  false
        
    -FolderPath <string>
        Source folder path.
        
        Required?                    true
        Position?                    0
        Default value                
        Accept pipeline input?       true (ByValue)
        Accept wildcard characters?  false
        
    -FolderID <int>
        Source folder ID.
        
        Required?                    true
        Position?                    0
        Default value                0
        Accept pipeline input?       true (ByValue)
        Accept wildcard characters?  false
        
    -FolderLevel <int>
        Level of folders to return access control for. Zero is the default which returns all access control entries for entire folder structure. Use FolderLevel of one for source folder only.
        
        Required?                    false
        Position?                    1
        Default value                0
        Accept pipeline input?       false
        Accept wildcard characters?  false
        
    -ExportFilePathName <string>
        Used to specify local folder path and file name to export access control data to. Must be either .xlsx (Excel) or .sqlite (SQLite Database) file extension.
        
        Required?                    false
        Position?                    2
        Default value                
        Accept pipeline input?       false
        Accept wildcard characters?  false
        
    <CommonParameters>
        This cmdlet supports the common parameters: Verbose, Debug,
        ErrorAction, ErrorVariable, WarningAction, WarningVariable,
        OutBuffer, PipelineVariable, and OutVariable. For more information, see 
        about_CommonParameters (https:/go.microsoft.com/fwlink/?LinkID=113216). 
    
INPUTS
    PWPS_DAB.CommonTypes+ProjectWiseFolder
        Source folder object(s) from pipeline.
    
    System.String
        Source folder path.
    
    System.Int32
        Source folder ID.
    
    
OUTPUTS
    
    ----------  EXAMPLE 1  ----------
    
    #Example usage for exporting ALL access control from a project to a datatable by passing ONE InputFolder object.
    $accessControlObjects = Export-PWProjectAccessControl -InputFolder (Get-PWFolders -FolderPath 'PowerShell\PowerShell_Test' -JustOne) -Verbose
    
    ----------  EXAMPLE 2  ----------
    
    #Example usage for exporting ALL access control from a project to a datatable by passing a FolderPath.
    $accessControlObjects = Export-PWProjectAccessControl -FolderPath 'PowerShell\PowerShell_Test' -Verbose
    
    ----------  EXAMPLE 3  ----------
    
    #Example usage for exporting ALL access control from a project to a datatable by passing a Folder ID.
    $accessControlObjects = Export-PWProjectAccessControl -FolderID 69212 -Verbose
    
    ----------  EXAMPLE 4  ----------
    
    #Example usage for exporting access control from a project to a datatable. Only the first (source) folder's access control objects will be returned.
    $accessControlObjects = Export-PWProjectAccessControl -FolderPath 'PowerShell\PowerShell_Test' -FolderLevel 1 -Verbose
    
    ----------  EXAMPLE 5  ----------
    
    #Example usage for exporting access control from a project to a datatable. Only the first two folders levels access control objects will be returned.
    $accessControlObjects = Export-PWProjectAccessControl -FolderID 69212 -FolderLevel 2 -Verbose
    
    ----------  EXAMPLE 6  ----------
    
    #Example usage for exporting access control from a project to an Excel spreadsheet. All project access control will be exported using default values. Passing the InputFolder via the pipeline.
    Get-PWFolders -FolderPath 'PowerShell\PowerShell_Test' -JustOne | Export-PWProjectAccessControl -ExportFilePathName 'd:\temp\export\MyAccessControl.xlsx' -Verbose
    
    ----------  EXAMPLE 7  ----------
    
    #Example usage for exporting access control from a project to a SQLite database. All project access control will be exported. Passing the InputFolder via the pipeline.
    Get-PWFolders -FolderPath 'PowerShell\PowerShell_Test' -JustOne | Export-PWProjectAccessControl -FolderLevel 0 -ExportFilePathName 'd:\temp\export\MyAccessControl_01.sqlite' -Verbose
    
    ----------  EXAMPLE 8  ----------
    
    #Example usage for exporting access control from a project to a SQLite database. Only the access control objects for the first three folders levels will be exported. Passing the InputFolder via the pipeline.
    Get-PWFolders -FolderPath 'PowerShell\PowerShell_Test' -JustOne | Export-PWProjectAccessControl -FolderLevel 3 -ExportFilePathName 'd:\temp\export\MyAccessControl_02.sqlite' -Verbose
    
    
RELATED LINKS

## Get-DirectoryListing


NAME
    Get-DirectoryListing
    
SYNOPSIS
    Saves a report of all the documents and metadata contained in a folder path or in a saved search.
    
    
SYNTAX
    Get-DirectoryListing [-Path] <string> [[-Filter] <string>] [[-OutputFileName] <string>] [<CommonParameters>]
    
    
DESCRIPTION
    Saves a report of all the documents and metadata contained in a folder path or in a saved search. Includes audit trail as well as records from backup audit trail table.
    
    Include neither path nor search name to report on whole datasource. Probably not a good idea to include audit trail in that case.
    
    Use the recurse parameter to include all sub-folders in the report.
    

PARAMETERS
    -Path <string>
        Path to the folder or drive to report on (e.g. "D:\Backup", "\\server\\F$\Work").
        
        Required?                    true
        Position?                    0
        Default value                
        Accept pipeline input?       false
        Accept wildcard characters?  false
        
    -Filter <string>
        File filter (defaults to *).
        
        Required?                    false
        Position?                    1
        Default value                *
        Accept pipeline input?       false
        Accept wildcard characters?  false
        
    -OutputFileName <string>
        Full path to output XLSX or SQLiteDB file (e.g. "C:\temp\MyOutputfile.xlsx", "c:\temp\output.sqldb").
        
        Required?                    false
        Position?                    2
        Default value                
        Accept pipeline input?       false
        Accept wildcard characters?  false
        
    <CommonParameters>
        This cmdlet supports the common parameters: Verbose, Debug,
        ErrorAction, ErrorVariable, WarningAction, WarningVariable,
        OutBuffer, PipelineVariable, and OutVariable. For more information, see 
        about_CommonParameters (https:/go.microsoft.com/fwlink/?LinkID=113216). 
    
INPUTS
    
OUTPUTS
    
    ----------  EXAMPLE 1  ----------
    
    #Example usage for reporting on documents.
    #Will report on the documents ONLY in the folder identified by the folder path.
    Save-PWDocumentReport -ProjectWiseFolder "PWPS Connected Project Test 6\Projects 2\Project A" -OutputFileName "c:\\temp\\xmittalReport.xlsx"
    #Will report on the documents ONLY in the folder identified by the folder path. Will include audit trail and versions.
    Save-PWDocumentReport -ProjectWiseFolder "PWPS Connected Project Test 6\Projects 2\Project A" -IncludeVersions -IncludeAuditTrail -OutputFileName "c:\\temp\\xmittalReport.xlsx"
    #Will report on the documents in the folder and all sub-folders identified by the folder path. Will include audit trail and versions.
    Save-PWDocumentReport -ProjectWiseFolder "PWPS Connected Project Test 6\Projects 2\Project A" -IncludeVersions -Recurse -IncludeAuditTrail -OutputFileName "c:\\temp\\xmittalReport.xlsx"
    #Will report on the documents in the saved search including the audit trail (will only include versions if they are included in search)
    Save-PWDocumentReport -SearchName "60% Complete" -IncludeAuditTrail -OutputFileName "c:\\temp\\xmittalReport.xlsx"
    #Will report on the documents in the folder and all sub-folders identified by the folder path. Will include audit trail between the given dates, will include versions and will output to a SQLite database.
    Save-PWDocumentReport -ProjectWiseFolder "PWPS Connected Project Test 6\Projects 2\Project A" -IncludeVersions -Recurse -IncludeAuditTrail -OutputFileName "c:\\temp\\xmittalReport.sqlite" -AuditTrailRecordsStart 2015-01-01 -AuditTrailRecordEnd 2015-12-31
    
    
RELATED LINKS





--

## Get-PWConnectedProject


NAME
    Get-PWConnectedProject
    
SYNOPSIS
    Gets CONNECTED project from a rich project.
    
    
SYNTAX
    Get-PWConnectedProject [-InputFolder] <ProjectWiseFolder[]> [[-ConnectedProjectUser] <string>] [[-ConnectedProjectPassword] <string>] [-Token] <string> [<CommonParameters>]
    
    
DESCRIPTION
    Takes an array of ProjectWiseFolders and returns connected project objects.
    

PARAMETERS
    -InputFolder <ProjectWiseFolder[]>
        Array of ProjectWise folders from pipeline.
        
        Required?                    true
        Position?                    0
        Default value                PWPS_DAB.CommonTypes+ProjectWiseFolder[]
        Accept pipeline input?       true (ByValue)
        Accept wildcard characters?  false
        
    -ConnectedProjectUser <string>
        Obsolete.
        
        Required?                    false
        Position?                    1
        Default value                
        Accept pipeline input?       false
        Accept wildcard characters?  false
        
    -ConnectedProjectPassword <string>
        Obsolete.
        
        Required?                    false
        Position?                    2
        Default value                
        Accept pipeline input?       false
        Accept wildcard characters?  false
        
    -Token <string>
        Pass base 64 encoded token from Get-PWConnectionClientToken (do not use -UseRelyingParty) or from Get-PWNonFederatedLoginToken -CreateWebToken.
        
        Required?                    true
        Position?                    3
        Default value                
        Accept pipeline input?       false
        Accept wildcard characters?  false
        
    <CommonParameters>
        This cmdlet supports the common parameters: Verbose, Debug,
        ErrorAction, ErrorVariable, WarningAction, WarningVariable,
        OutBuffer, PipelineVariable, and OutVariable. For more information, see 
        about_CommonParameters (https:/go.microsoft.com/fwlink/?LinkID=113216). 
    
INPUTS
    PWPS_DAB.CommonTypes+ProjectWiseFolder[]
        Array of ProjectWise folders from pipeline.
    
    
OUTPUTS
    
    ----------  EXAMPLE 1  ----------
    
    #Example usage for getting the CONNECTED project for each rich project in a tree.
    New-PWLogin Server:DSN
    #Get all the rich projects in this tree and pipe to this cmdlet
    $rps = Get-PWRichProjects -FolderPath "PWPS Connected Project Test 6\Projects 2"
    #foreach rich project, get the Connected Project ID
    foreach ($rp in $rps) 
    {
    write-host $rp
    Get-PWConnectedProject $rp 
    }
    
    
RELATED LINKS

    Get-PWConnectedProjectUsersOIDC

    Gets Connected Project Users.

    Get-PWConnectedProjectUsersOIDC [[-InputFolder] <ProjectWiseFolder[]>] [-OIDCToken] <OIDCAuthToken> [[-ConnectedProjectIds] <string[]>] [[-OutputFile] <string>] [<CommonParameters>]
    
    
DESCRIPTION
    

PARAMETERS
    -InputFolder <ProjectWiseFolder[]>
        Array of ProjectWise folders from pipeline.
        
        Required?                    false
        Position?                    0
        Default value                PWPS_DAB.CommonTypes+ProjectWiseFolder[]
        Accept pipeline input?       true (ByValue)
        Accept wildcard characters?  false
        
    -OIDCToken <OIDCAuthToken>
        Pass the whole OIDC Token object returned from Get-OIDCToken. Required.
        
        Required?                    true
        Position?                    1
        Default value                
        Accept pipeline input?       false
        Accept wildcard characters?  false
        
    -ConnectedProjectIds <string[]>
        List of Connected Project Ids.
        
        Required?                    false
        Position?                    2
        Default value                System.String[]
        Accept pipeline input?       false
        Accept wildcard characters?  false
        
    -OutputFile <string>
        Pass access_token part of OIDC Token returned from Get-OIDCToken cmdlet. Required.
        
        Required?                    false
        Position?                    3
        Default value                
        Accept pipeline input?       false
        Accept wildcard characters?  false
        
    <CommonParameters>
        This cmdlet supports the common parameters: Verbose, Debug,
        ErrorAction, ErrorVariable, WarningAction, WarningVariable,
        OutBuffer, PipelineVariable, and OutVariable. For more information, see 
        about_CommonParameters (https:/go.microsoft.com/fwlink/?LinkID=113216).

OUTPUTS

## Get-PWDMIncomingRFIs


NAME
    Get-PWDMIncomingRFIs
    
SYNOPSIS
    Generates a list containing all Incoming RFIs in the CONNECTed project associated with the rich projects passed in.
    
    
SYNTAX
    Get-PWDMIncomingRFIs [[-InputFolders] <ProjectWiseFolder[]>] [[-ConnectedProjectId] <string>] [[-ConnectedProjectUser] <string>] [[-ConnectedProjectPassword] <string>] [[-Company] <string>] [[-IssuerEmail] <string>] [[-UseCheckProject] <SwitchParameter>] [-ConnectToken] <string> 
    [[-ReceivedSince] <DateTime>] [<CommonParameters>]
    
    
DESCRIPTION
    Generates a list containing all Incoming RFIs in the CONNECTed project associated with the rich projects passed in.
    

PARAMETERS
    -InputFolders <ProjectWiseFolder[]>
        Array of ProjectWise folders from pipeline. These folders will be included in report if they are rich projects and have CONNECTed projects.
        
        Required?                    false
        Position?                    0
        Default value                PWPS_DAB.CommonTypes+ProjectWiseFolder[]
        Accept pipeline input?       true (ByValue)
        Accept wildcard characters?  false
        
    -ConnectedProjectId <string>
        Path to the rich project from which we'll find the associated CONNECTed project.
        
        Required?                    false
        Position?                    1
        Default value                
        Accept pipeline input?       false
        Accept wildcard characters?  false
        
    -ConnectedProjectUser <string>
        Not used.
        
        Required?                    false
        Position?                    2
        Default value                
        Accept pipeline input?       false
        Accept wildcard characters?  false
        
    -ConnectedProjectPassword <string>
        Not used.
        
        Required?                    false
        Position?                    3
        Default value                
        Accept pipeline input?       false
        Accept wildcard characters?  false
        
    -Company <string>
        If set, will filter RFIs by Company.
        
        Required?                    false
        Position?                    4
        Default value                
        Accept pipeline input?       false
        Accept wildcard characters?  false
        
    -IssuerEmail <string>
        If set, will filter RFIs by Issuer email.
        
        Required?                    false
        Position?                    5
        Default value                
        Accept pipeline input?       false
        Accept wildcard characters?  false
        
    -UseCheckProject <SwitchParameter>
        If set, will use CheckProject instead of GetProjectByBCKey.
        
        Required?                    false
        Position?                    6
        Default value                False
        Accept pipeline input?       false
        Accept wildcard characters?  false
        
    -ConnectToken <string>
        Connect token to use.
        
        Required?                    true
        Position?                    7
        Default value                
        Accept pipeline input?       false
        Accept wildcard characters?  false
        
    -ReceivedSince <DateTime>
        Received since date. Defaults to Jan 1, 2015.
        
        Required?                    false
        Position?                    8
        Default value                1/1/2015 12:00:00 AM
        Accept pipeline input?       false
        Accept wildcard characters?  false
        
    <CommonParameters>
        This cmdlet supports the common parameters: Verbose, Debug,
        ErrorAction, ErrorVariable, WarningAction, WarningVariable,
        OutBuffer, PipelineVariable, and OutVariable. For more information, see 
        about_CommonParameters (https:/go.microsoft.com/fwlink/?LinkID=113216). 
    
INPUTS
    PWPS_DAB.CommonTypes+ProjectWiseFolder[]
        Array of ProjectWise folders from pipeline. These folders will be included in report if they are rich projects and have CONNECTed projects.
    
    
OUTPUTS
    
    ----------  EXAMPLE 1  ----------
    
    #Example usage for reporting on incoming RFIs for CONNECTED projects.
    $rps=Get-PWRichProjects
    GetPWDMIncomingRFIs $rps
