## Get-PWDMIncomingRFIsWithProperties


NAME
    Get-PWDMIncomingRFIsWithProperties
    
SYNOPSIS
    Generates a list containing all Incoming RFIs in the rich project's CONNECTed project issued since the given date.
    
    
SYNTAX
    Get-PWDMIncomingRFIsWithProperties [-ConnectedProjectId] <string> [-ConnectToken] <string> [[-IssuedSince] <DateTime>] [<CommonParameters>]
    
    
DESCRIPTION
    Generates a list containing all Incoming RFIs in the rich project's CONNECTed project issued since the given date.
    

PARAMETERS
    -ConnectedProjectId <string>
        Project ID to query.
        
        Required?                    true
        Position?                    0
        Default value                
        Accept pipeline input?       true (ByValue)
        Accept wildcard characters?  false
        
    -ConnectToken <string>
        Service Account Token.
        
        Required?                    true
        Position?                    1
        Default value                
        Accept pipeline input?       true (ByValue)
        Accept wildcard characters?  false
        
    -IssuedSince <DateTime>
        Date since which RFI was issued.
        
        Required?                    false
        Position?                    2
        Default value                1/1/2015 12:00:00 AM
        Accept pipeline input?       true (ByValue)
        Accept wildcard characters?  false
        
    <CommonParameters>
        This cmdlet supports the common parameters: Verbose, Debug,
        ErrorAction, ErrorVariable, WarningAction, WarningVariable,
        OutBuffer, PipelineVariable, and OutVariable. For more information, see 
        about_CommonParameters (https:/go.microsoft.com/fwlink/?LinkID=113216). 
    
INPUTS
    System.String
        Project ID to query.
    
    System.String
        Service Account Token.
    
    System.DateTime
        Date since which RFI was issued.
    
    
OUTPUTS
    
    ----------  EXAMPLE 1  ----------
    
    $folder = Get-PWFolderByURN 'pw://decide-pwce-us.bentley.com:decide-pwce-us-10/Documents/P{c654ea13-d144-4053-99d4-41f092399e56}/'
    $webToken = Get-PWNonFederatedLoginToken -UserName dave.brumbaugh@eagle.bentley.com -Password (ConvertTo-SecureString xxx -AsPlainText -Force) -CreateWebToken
    Get-PWDMIncomingRFIsWithProperties -ConnectedProjectId $folder.ConnectedProjectId -ConnectToken $webToken -IssuedSince '2018-01-01'

    ----------  EXAMPLE 1  ----------
    
    #Example usage for returning the containing submittals/transmittals for a collection of documents.
    $folder = Get-PWFolderByURN 'pw://decide-pwce-us.bentley.com:decide-pwce-us-10/Documents/P{ce771b2e-bfed-46de-ae04-41f9d3fdef01}/'
    $docs = Get-PWDocumentsBySearchExtended -FolderPath $folder.FullPath -GetVersionsToo -FileName %.pdf
    $token = Get-PWConnectionClientToken
    $trans = Get-PWDMTransmittalsForDocuments $docs -Token $token
    New-XLSXWorkbook $trans -OutputFileName c:\temp\LatestTransmittals.xlsx

## Get-PWDocumentReportDataTable


NAME
    Get-PWDocumentReportDataTable
    
SYNOPSIS
    Output a report of all the documents and metadata contained in a folder path or in a saved search.
    
    
SYNTAX
    Get-PWDocumentReportDataTable [[-ProjectWiseFolder] <string>] [[-SearchName] <string>] [[-DocumentName] <string>] [[-FileName] <string>] [[-FolderId] <int>] [[-IncludeVersions] <SwitchParameter>] [[-IncludeAuditTrail] <SwitchParameter>] [[-Recurse] <SwitchParameter>] 
    [[-AuditTrailRecordsStart] <DateTime>] [[-AuditTrailRecordsEnd] <DateTime>] [[-Personal] <SwitchParameter>] [[-ExcludeSecondaryAuditTrail] <SwitchParameter>] [<CommonParameters>]
    
    
DESCRIPTION
    Output a report of all the documents and metadata contained in a folder path or in a saved search. Includes audit trail as well as records from backup audit trail table.
    
    Include neither path nor search name to report on whole datasource. Probably not a good idea to include audit trail in that case.
    
    Use the recurse parameter to include all sub-folders in the report.
    

PARAMETERS
    -ProjectWiseFolder <string>
        Path to the folder to report on (e.g. "PWPS Connected Project Test 6\Projects 2\Project A").
        
        Required?                    false
        Position?                    0
        Default value                
        Accept pipeline input?       false
        Accept wildcard characters?  false
        
    -SearchName <string>
        Name of saved search to report on (e.g. "60% Complete").
        
        Required?                    false
        Position?                    1
        Default value                
        Accept pipeline input?       false
        Accept wildcard characters?  false
        
    -FolderId <int>
        Folder Id of folder to report on.
        
        Required?                    false
        Position?                    2
        Default value                0
        Accept pipeline input?       false
        Accept wildcard characters?  false
        
    -IncludeVersions <SwitchParameter>
        Include this switch to report on versions.
        
        Required?                    false
        Position?                    3
        Default value                False
        Accept pipeline input?       false
        Accept wildcard characters?  false
        
    -IncludeAuditTrail <SwitchParameter>
        Include this switch to include the audit trail.
        
        Required?                    false
        Position?                    4
        Default value                False
        Accept pipeline input?       false
        Accept wildcard characters?  false
        
    -Recurse <SwitchParameter>
        When included, reports on all the documents within the specified folder and all sub-folders. Note that this is a change from the original behavior.
        
        Required?                    false
        Position?                    5
        Default value                False
        Accept pipeline input?       false
        Accept wildcard characters?  false
        
    -AuditTrailRecordsStart <DateTime>
        If set, include audit trail records newer than this date.
        
        Required?                    false
        Position?                    6
        Default value                1/1/0001 12:00:00 AM
        Accept pipeline input?       false
        Accept wildcard characters?  false
        
    -AuditTrailRecordsEnd <DateTime>
        If set, include audit trail records older than this date.
        
        Required?                    false
        Position?                    7
        Default value                1/1/0001 12:00:00 AM
        Accept pipeline input?       false
        Accept wildcard characters?  false
        
    -Personal <SwitchParameter>
        Look for a personal search.
        
        Required?                    false
        Position?                    8
        Default value                False
        Accept pipeline input?       false
        Accept wildcard characters?  false
        
    -ExcludeSecondaryAuditTrail <SwitchParameter>
        Don't include secondary audit trail records. Sometimes required for performance.
        
        Required?                    false
        Position?                    9
        Default value                False
        Accept pipeline input?       false
        Accept wildcard characters?  false
        
    -DocumentName <string>
        Document name. Supports % wild card.
        
        Required?                    false
        Position?                    10
        Default value                
        Accept pipeline input?       false
        Accept wildcard characters?  false
        
    -FileName <string>
        File name. Supports % wild card.
        
        Required?                    false
        Position?                    11
        Default value                
        Accept pipeline input?       false
        Accept wildcard characters?  false
        
    <CommonParameters>
        This cmdlet supports the common parameters: Verbose, Debug,
        ErrorAction, ErrorVariable, WarningAction, WarningVariable,
        OutBuffer, PipelineVariable, and OutVariable. For more information, see 
        about_CommonParameters (https:/go.microsoft.com/fwlink/?LinkID=113216). 
    
INPUTS
    
OUTPUTS
    System.Data.DataTable[]
    
    
    ----------  EXAMPLE 1  ----------
    
    #Will report on the documents ONLY in the folder identified by the folder path
    Get-PWDocumentReportDataTable -ProjectWiseFolder "PWPS Connected Project Test 6\Projects 2\Project A"
    #Will report on the documents ONLY in the folder identified by the folder path, and will include audit trail and versions.
    Get-PWDocumentReportDataTable -ProjectWiseFolder "PWPS Connected Project Test 6\Projects 2\Project A" -IncludeAuditTrail -IncludeVersions
    #Will report on the documents in the folder identified by the folder path and all sub-folders.
    Get-PWDocumentReportDataTable -ProjectWiseFolder "PWPS Connected Project Test 6\Projects 2\Project A" -Recurse
    #Will report on the documents in the folder identified by the folder path and all sub-folders. Will include audit trail and versions.
    Get-PWDocumentReportDataTable -ProjectWiseFolder "PWPS Connected Project Test 6\Projects 2\Project A" -Recurse -IncludeAuditTrail -IncludeVersions
    #Will report on the documents ONLY in the folder identified by the folder path
    Get-PWDocumentReportDataTable -ProjectWiseFolder "PWPS Connected Project Test 6\Projects 2\Project A"
    #Will report on the documents in the saved search.
    Get-PWDocumentReportDataTable -SearchName "60% Complete"
    #Will report on the documents in the saved search including the audit trail (will only include versions if they are included in search)
    Get-PWDocumentReportDataTable -SearchName "60% Complete" -IncludeAuditTrail
    #Will report on the documents in the folder and all sub-folders identified by the folder path. Will include audit trail between the given dates and will include versions.
    Get-PWDocumentReportDataTable -ProjectWiseFolder "PWPS Connected Project Test 6\Projects 2\Project A" -IncludeVersions -Recurse -IncludeAuditTrail -AuditTrailRecordsStart 2015-01-01 -AuditTrailRecordEnd 2015-12-31

    #Example usages for searching for documents.
    Import-Module pwps_dab
    New-PWLogin Server:DSN 
    #Get the documents in just this folder (and their versions) where the file name pattern matches %.pdf
    Get-PWDocumentsBySearch -FolderPath "Test 6\Projects 2" -GetVersionsToo -JustThisFolder -Filename '%.pdf'

    #Get the documents returned by the saved search (note path definition) from a search defined in a rich project 
    Get-PWDocumentsBySearch -SearchName "Project Searches\PDF Search made by PowerShell" -PathOfSearchProject "Projects\Project 01"

    Get-PWDocumentsBySearchExtended -FolderPath "Test 6\Projects 2" -Filename '%.pdf' -States "Draft","Pending Approval" -Status CheckedOut -ColumnsToReturn "PercentComplete","DrawingNumber" -ReturnDataTable

    #Get the active documents in this folder tree where the file name pattern matches %.pdf, is in one of the listed states and return the columns specified

    #Get the documents in this folder tree (and their versions) where the file name pattern matches %.pdf and 'Primary' is in the full-text index
    Get-PWDocumentsBySearchWithReturnColumns -FolderPath "Test 6\Projects 2" -Filename '%.pdf' -GetVersionsToo -States "Draft","Pending Approval" -SearchString "Primary" -ColumnsToReturn "PercentComplete","DrawingNumber"
    #Get the active documents in this folder tree matching these attributes where the file was updated after the given date
    Get-PWDocumentsBySearchWithReturnColumns -FolderPath "Test 6\Projects 2" -Attributes @{Name = 'Value'; Name2 = 'Value2' } -FileUpdatedAfter 2017-01-01
    #Get the active documents in this folder tree matching these attributes where the file was updated between the given dates
    Get-PWDocumentsBySearchWithReturnColumns -FolderPath "Test 6\Projects 2" -Attributes @{Name = 'Value'; Name2 = 'Value2' } -FileUpdatedAfter 2017-01-01 -FileUpdatedBefore 2017-02-01
    #Get the active documents in this folder tree where the file name pattern matches %.pdf, is in one of the listed states and return the columns specified in a DataTable
    Get-PWDocumentsBySearchWithReturnColumns -FolderPath "Test 6\Projects 2" -Filename '%.pdf' -States "Draft","Pending Approval" -ColumnsToReturn "PercentComplete","DrawingNumber" -ReturnDataTable

## Get-PWFolders


NAME
    Get-PWFolders
    
SYNOPSIS
    Gets a list of the folders in a given path or under a given folder ID.
    
    
SYNTAX
    Get-PWFolders [[-FolderPath] <string>] [[-FolderID] <int>] [[-FolderName] <string>] [[-JustOne] <SwitchParameter>] [[-BypassSearchAssembly] <SwitchParameter>] [[-OutputFileName] <string>] [[-Slow] <SwitchParameter>] [[-PopulatePaths] <SwitchParameter>] [<CommonParameters>]
    
    
DESCRIPTION
    Takes a folder ID or folder path and enumerates all the folders beneath it in the tree.
    

PARAMETERS
    -FolderID <int>
        Folder ID for enumerating sub-folders.
        
        Required?                    false
        Position?                    1
        Default value                0
        Accept pipeline input?       false
        Accept wildcard characters?  false
        
    -FolderPath <string>
        Folder path for enumerating sub-folders.
        
        Required?                    false
        Position?                    0
        Default value                
        Accept pipeline input?       false
        Accept wildcard characters?  false
        
    -FolderName <string>
        Folder name for enumerating folders. Instructs to search for matching folder names.
        
        Required?                    false
        Position?                    2
        Default value                
        Accept pipeline input?       false
        Accept wildcard characters?  false
        
    -JustOne <SwitchParameter>
        Just return specified folder.
        
        Required?                    false
        Position?                    3
        Default value                False
        Accept pipeline input?       false
        Accept wildcard characters?  false
        
    -BypassSearchAssembly <SwitchParameter>
        OBSOLETE. Not used.
        
        Required?                    false
        Position?                    4
        Default value                False
        Accept pipeline input?       false
        Accept wildcard characters?  false
        
    -OutputFileName <string>
        Provide if you desire a report.
        
        Required?                    false
        Position?                    5
        Default value                
        Accept pipeline input?       false
        Accept wildcard characters?  false
        
    -Slow <SwitchParameter>
        Specify to populate folder path and project properties. Can take a long time for a dense folder tree.
        
        Required?                    false
        Position?                    6
        Default value                False
        Accept pipeline input?       false
        Accept wildcard characters?  false
        
    -PopulatePaths <SwitchParameter>
        Populate paths. Should be more performant than -Slow though somewhat less data is returned.
        
        Required?                    false
        Position?                    7
        Default value                False
        Accept pipeline input?       false
        Accept wildcard characters?  false
        
    <CommonParameters>
        This cmdlet supports the common parameters: Verbose, Debug,
        ErrorAction, ErrorVariable, WarningAction, WarningVariable,
        OutBuffer, PipelineVariable, and OutVariable. For more information, see 
        about_CommonParameters (https:/go.microsoft.com/fwlink/?LinkID=113216). 
    
INPUTS
    
OUTPUTS
    
    ----------  EXAMPLE 1  ----------
    
    #Example usage for getting all the folders in a given folder path.
    #Get all the folders in this tree
    $folders = Get-PWFolders -FolderPath "PWPS Connected Project Test 6\Projects 2"
    #Get all the folders in this tree with paths populated
    $folders = Get-PWFolders -FolderPath "PWPS Connected Project Test 6\Projects 2" -PopulatePaths
    #Get all the folders in this tree with paths and all data populated
    $folders = Get-PWFolders -FolderPath "PWPS Connected Project Test 6\Projects 2" -Slow
    #Get all folders with name matching the pattern (fast)
    $folders = Get-PWFolders -FolderName "%project%"
    #to get the full paths populated, do this (slow)
    $folders.GetFullPath()
    
    
RELATED LINKS

## Get-PWFoldersByAccessMember


NAME
    Get-PWFoldersByAccessMember
    
SYNOPSIS
    Get-PWFoldersByAccessMember is used to get a list of folder objects which has a member explicitly set in its access control.
    
    
SYNTAX
    Get-PWFoldersByAccessMember [[-InputFolder] <ProjectWiseFolder[]>] [-MemberType] <string> [-MemberName] <string> [<CommonParameters>]
    
    Get-PWFoldersByAccessMember [-MemberType] <string> [-MemberName] <string> [-SearchEntireDatasource <SwitchParameter>] [<CommonParameters>]
    
    
DESCRIPTION
    Returns an array of ProjectWise Folder objects which the membername explicitly set in its access control. If no ProjectWise folders are passed to the InputFolder parameter, the user will be prompted to complete the process unless the -SearchEntireDatasource switch parameter is 
    included.
    

PARAMETERS
    -InputFolder <ProjectWiseFolder[]>
        
        Required?                    false
        Position?                    0
        Default value                PWPS_DAB.CommonTypes+ProjectWiseFolder[]
        Accept pipeline input?       true (ByValue)
        Accept wildcard characters?  false
        
    -MemberType <string>
        
        Required?                    true
        Position?                    1
        Default value                
        Accept pipeline input?       false
        Accept wildcard characters?  false
        
    -MemberName <string>
        
        Required?                    true
        Position?                    2
        Default value                
        Accept pipeline input?       false
        Accept wildcard characters?  false
        
    -SearchEntireDatasource <SwitchParameter>
        
        Required?                    false
        Position?                    named
        Default value                False
        Accept pipeline input?       false
        Accept wildcard characters?  false
        
    <CommonParameters>
        This cmdlet supports the common parameters: Verbose, Debug,
        ErrorAction, ErrorVariable, WarningAction, WarningVariable,
        OutBuffer, PipelineVariable, and OutVariable. For more information, see 
        about_CommonParameters (https:/go.microsoft.com/fwlink/?LinkID=113216). 
    
INPUTS
    PWPS_DAB.CommonTypes+ProjectWiseFolder[]
    
    
OUTPUTS
    
    ----------  EXAMPLE 1  ----------
    
    #Example usage getting projects / folders with specified member in its access control.
    The following example will return an array of ProjectWise Folder objects from the folders being passed via the pipeline, which have the 'Read_Only' userlist applied to its access control. 
    $pwFolders = Get-PWFolders -FolderPath 'Projects' | 
    Get-PWFoldersByAccessMember -MemberType 'UserList' -MemberName 'Read_Only' -Verbose
    
    ----------  EXAMPLE 2  ----------
    
    #Example usage getting projects / folders with specified member in its access control.
    The following example will return an array of ProjectWise Folder objects from the folders being passed, which have the 'Read_Only' userlist applied to its access control. 
    $pwFolders = Get-PWFolders -FolderPath 'Projects'
    Get-PWFoldersByAccessMember -InputFolder $pwFolders -MemberType 'UserList' -MemberName 'Read_Only' -Verbose
    
    ----------  EXAMPLE 3  ----------
    
    #Example usage getting projects / folders with specified member in its access control.
    The following example will return an array of ProjectWise Folder objects from the ENTIRE datasource, which have the 'PowerShell Users' group applied to its access control. The user will be prompted to complete the process.
    Get-PWFoldersByAccessMember -MemberType 'Group' -MemberName 'PowerShell Users' -Verbose
    
    ----------  EXAMPLE 4  ----------
    
    #Example usage getting projects / folders with specified member in its access control.
    The following example will return an array of ProjectWise Folder objects from the ENTIRE datasource, which have the 'PowerShell Users' group applied to its access control. 
    Get-PWFoldersByAccessMember -MemberType 'Group' -MemberName 'PowerShell Users' -SearchEntireDatasource -Verbose
    
    
RELATED LINKS

## Get-PWFolderSecurity


NAME
    Get-PWFolderSecurity
    
SYNOPSIS
    The Get-PWFolderSecurity cmdlet is used to get access control information for a specific project/folder.
    
    
SYNTAX
    Get-PWFolderSecurity [-InputFolder] <ProjectWiseFolder[]> [<CommonParameters>]
    
    
DESCRIPTION
    The Get-PWFolderSecurity cmdlet is used to get access control information for a specific project/folder. This cmdlet will return a datatable specifying the project/folder access control type, name, security type (document or project/folder), the access control settings (mask value), 
    and if it is inheriting access control, where from. If nothing is listed in the Inherited_From column, that indicates the access settings are applied directly to the project/folder. ProjectName | Type | Name | SecurityType | Access_Control_Settings | Workflow | State 
    |Inheriting_From | FullPath ------------|-----------|-----------------|-----------------|---------------------------|--------------|-------------|-------------------|---------------------- DWGs | user | admin | Project/Folder | 65535 | | | Projects | Projects\DWGs DWGs | group | 
    administrators | Project/Folder | 65535 | | | Projects | Projects\DWGs DWGs | userlist | all_users | Project/Folder | 6 | | | Projects | Projects\DWGs DWGs | user | admin | Document | 65535 | Workflow 1 | Initiated | | Projects\DWGS DWGs | userlist | all_users | Document | 190 | | | 
    | Projects\DWGs
    

PARAMETERS
    -InputFolder <ProjectWiseFolder[]>
        
        Required?                    true
        Position?                    0
        Default value                PWPS_DAB.CommonTypes+ProjectWiseFolder[]
        Accept pipeline input?       true (ByValue)
        Accept wildcard characters?  false
        
    <CommonParameters>
        This cmdlet supports the common parameters: Verbose, Debug,
        ErrorAction, ErrorVariable, WarningAction, WarningVariable,
        OutBuffer, PipelineVariable, and OutVariable. For more information, see 
        about_CommonParameters (https:/go.microsoft.com/fwlink/?LinkID=113216). 
    
INPUTS
    PWPS_DAB.CommonTypes+ProjectWiseFolder[]
    
    
OUTPUTS
    
    ----------  EXAMPLE 1  ----------
    
    #Example usage getting project/folder access control.
    The following will return a datatable containing the access control of the specified project/folder.
       Get-PWFolders -FolderPath 'projects' -JustOne -Slow | Get-PWFolderSecurity

DESCRIPTION

        Required?                    false
        Position?                    0
        Default value                
        Accept pipeline input?       false
        Accept wildcard characters?  false
        
    -WorkspaceType <string>

        "Application", "Customer", "Site", "Workspace", "WorkSet", "Project", "Role", "User"
        
        Required?                    false
        Position?                    0
        Default value

        Accept wildcard characters?  false

## Get-PWReferenceCountReportForDocuments


NAME
    Get-PWReferenceCountReportForDocuments
    
SYNOPSIS
    Get XLSX report or SQLite or straight DataTable that counts unique references documents passed in pipeline.
    
    
SYNTAX
    Get-PWReferenceCountReportForDocuments [-InputDocument] <ProjectWiseDocument[]> [[-OutputFilePath] <string>] [<CommonParameters>]
    
    
DESCRIPTION
    

PARAMETERS
    -InputDocument <ProjectWiseDocument[]>
        Documents from pipeline.
        
        Required?                    true
        Position?                    0
        Default value                
        Accept pipeline input?       true (ByValue)
        Accept wildcard characters?  false
        
    -OutputFilePath <string>
        Full path to output file (XLSX or SQLite). Exclude just to return data tables.
        
        Required?                    false
        Position?                    1
        Default value                
        Accept pipeline input?       true (ByValue)
        Accept wildcard characters?  false
        
    <CommonParameters>
        This cmdlet supports the common parameters: Verbose, Debug,
        ErrorAction, ErrorVariable, WarningAction, WarningVariable,
        OutBuffer, PipelineVariable, and OutVariable. For more information, see 
        about_CommonParameters (https:/go.microsoft.com/fwlink/?LinkID=113216). 
    
INPUTS
    PWPS_DAB.CommonTypes+ProjectWiseDocument[]
        Documents from pipeline.
    
    System.String
        Full path to output file (XLSX or SQLite). Exclude just to return data tables.
    
    
OUTPUTS
    System.Data.DataTable
    
    
    ----------  EXAMPLE 1  ----------
    
    #use a variable to pass multiple documents. Using a pipe ('|') will cause each document to be processed individually. Ususally not what you want.
    $documents = Get-PWDocumentsBySearch -FolderPath 'Top Level\Sub-Folder'
    Get-PWReferenceCountReportForDocuments $documents  -OutputFilePath c:\temp\References.xlsx
    
    ----------  EXAMPLE 2  ----------
    
    #Use data table to populate SQL Server Database
    $cn = new-object System.Data.SqlClient.SqlConnection("Data Source=brumd09515rem;User ID=sa;Password=pwd;Initial Catalog=BulkCopyTest")
    $cn.Open()    
    $bc = new-object ("System.Data.SqlClient.SqlBulkCopy") $cn
    $bc.DestinationTableName = "dbo.References_Table"
    $documents = Get-PWDocumentsBySearch -FolderPath 'Top Level\Sub-Folder'
    $dtable=Get-PWReferenceCountReportForDocuments $documents
    $bc.WriteToServer($dtable)
    $cn.Close()
    
    
RELATED LINKS

## Get-PWReferenceFiles

SYNTAX
    Get-PWReferenceFiles [-InputDocument] <ProjectWiseDocument[]> [[-ReferenceLevel] <int>] [[-GetAttributes] <SwitchParameter>] [<CommonParameters>]
    
    
DESCRIPTION
    #Search for documents and return immediate child documents.
    
    Get-PWDocumentsBySearch -SearchName "Documents in Released State" | Get-PWReferenceFiles -ReferenceLevel 0
    
    #Search for documents in folder tree and return all nested references and fill in folder paths and retrieve attributes.
    
    Get-PWDocumentsBySearch -FolderPath "Project A\Files to Version" | Get-PWReferenceFiles -GetAttributes
    

PARAMETERS
    -InputDocument <ProjectWiseDocument[]>
        Array of documents passed on pipeline like from Get-PWDocumentsBySearch.
        
        Required?                    true
        Position?                    0
        Default value                
        Accept pipeline input?       true (ByValue)
        Accept wildcard characters?  false
        
    -ReferenceLevel <int>
        Level of nested references to return. Defaults to all nested references.
        
        Required?                    false
        Position?                    1
        Default value                -1
        Accept pipeline input?       false
        Accept wildcard characters?  false
        
    -GetAttributes <SwitchParameter>
        Return attributes for references. Takes longer to populate the list.
        
        Required?                    false
        Position?                    2
        Default value                False
        Accept pipeline input?       false
        Accept wildcard characters?  false
        
    <CommonParameters>
        This cmdlet supports the common parameters: Verbose, Debug,
        ErrorAction, ErrorVariable, WarningAction, WarningVariable,
        OutBuffer, PipelineVariable, and OutVariable. For more information, see 
        about_CommonParameters (https:/go.microsoft.com/fwlink/?LinkID=113216). 
    
INPUTS
    PWPS_DAB.CommonTypes+ProjectWiseDocument[]
        Array of documents passed on pipeline like from Get-PWDocumentsBySearch.
    
    
OUTPUTS
    
    ----------  EXAMPLE 1  ----------
    
    #Search for documents and return immediate child documents.
    Get-PWDocumentsBySearch -SearchName "Documents in Released State" | Get-PWReferenceFiles -ReferenceLevel 0
    #Search for documents in folder tree and return all nested references and fill in folder paths and retrieve attributes.

## Get-PWReferenceReportForDocuments


NAME
    Get-PWReferenceReportForDocuments
    
SYNOPSIS
    Get XLSX report or SQLite or straight DataTable for all references in documents passed in pipeline.
    
    
SYNTAX
    Get-PWReferenceReportForDocuments [-InputDocument] <ProjectWiseDocument[]> [[-OutputFilePath] <string>] [<CommonParameters>]
    
    
DESCRIPTION
    

PARAMETERS
    -InputDocument <ProjectWiseDocument[]>
        Documents from pipeline.
        
        Required?                    true
        Position?                    0
        Default value                
        Accept pipeline input?       true (ByValue)
        Accept wildcard characters?  false
        
    -OutputFilePath <string>
        Full path to output file (XLSX or SQLite). Exclude just to return data tables.
        
        Required?                    false
        Position?                    1
        Default value                
        Accept pipeline input?       true (ByValue)
        Accept wildcard characters?  false
        
    <CommonParameters>
        This cmdlet supports the common parameters: Verbose, Debug,
        ErrorAction, ErrorVariable, WarningAction, WarningVariable,
        OutBuffer, PipelineVariable, and OutVariable. For more information, see 
        about_CommonParameters (https:/go.microsoft.com/fwlink/?LinkID=113216). 
    
INPUTS
    PWPS_DAB.CommonTypes+ProjectWiseDocument[]
        Documents from pipeline.
    
    System.String
        Full path to output file (XLSX or SQLite). Exclude just to return data tables.
    
    
OUTPUTS
    System.Data.DataTable
    
    
    ----------  EXAMPLE 1  ----------
    
    #use a variable to pass multiple documents. Using a pipe ('|') will cause each document to be processed individually. Ususally not what you want.
    $documents = Get-PWDocumentsBySearch -FolderPath 'Top Level\Sub-Folder'
    Get-PWReferenceReportForDocuments $documents  -OutputFilePath c:\temp\References.xlsx
    
    ----------  EXAMPLE 2  ----------
    
    #Use data table to populate SQL Server Database
    $cn = new-object System.Data.SqlClient.SqlConnection("Data Source=brumd09515rem;User ID=sa;Password=pwd;Initial Catalog=BulkCopyTest")
    $cn.Open()    
    $bc = new-object ("System.Data.SqlClient.SqlBulkCopy") $cn
    $bc.DestinationTableName = "dbo.References_Table"
    $documents = Get-PWDocumentsBySearch -FolderPath 'Top Level\Sub-Folder'
    $dtable=Get-PWReferenceReportForDocuments $documents
    $bc.WriteToServer($dtable)
    $cn.Close()
    
    
RELATED LINKS





--

## Get-PWReferenceReportForFolder


NAME
    Get-PWReferenceReportForFolder
    
SYNOPSIS
    Get XLSX report or SQLite DB or straight datatable for all references in the given folder and its children.
    
    
SYNTAX
    Get-PWReferenceReportForFolder [[-FolderPath] <string>] [[-OutputFilePath] <string>] [[-WholeDatasource] <SwitchParameter>] [<CommonParameters>]
    
    
DESCRIPTION

        Position?                    0
        Default value                
        Accept pipeline input?       false
        Accept wildcard characters?  false
        
    -OutputFilePath <string>

        Required?                    false
        Position?                    1
        Default value                
        Accept pipeline input?       false

        Position?                    2
        Default value                False
        Accept pipeline input?       false
        Accept wildcard characters?  false

OUTPUTS
    System.Data.DataTable

    Get-PWRenditionProfileComponentDestinationDatasource [-OutputDestinationFolderName] <string> [<CommonParameters>]
    
    
DESCRIPTION
    Get-PWRenditionProfileComponentDestinationDatasource returns destination datasource name associated with the provided output destination folder name. To see a list of available output destination folder names, you can issue the cmdlet Get-PWRenditionDestinations. You can also see 
    these with ProjectWise Administrator under Renditions, Rendition Profile Components, Output Destination Folders. If you double click on one of these a dialog will be presented. Of this dialog has an Options tab, the first item should be Datasource: This is what this cmdlet will be 
    returning.
    

PARAMETERS
    -OutputDestinationFolderName <string>
        Output destination folder name. Must exist.
        
        Required?                    true
        Position?                    0
        Default value                
        Accept pipeline input?       false
        Accept wildcard characters?  false
        
    <CommonParameters>
        This cmdlet supports the common parameters: Verbose, Debug,
        ErrorAction, ErrorVariable, WarningAction, WarningVariable,
        OutBuffer, PipelineVariable, and OutVariable. For more information, see 
        about_CommonParameters (https:/go.microsoft.com/fwlink/?LinkID=113216). 
    
INPUTS
    
OUTPUTS
    
    ----------  EXAMPLE 1  ----------
    
    Returns the destination datasource name associated with "Renditions Folder".
    Get-PWRenditionProfileComponentDestinationDatasource -OutputDestinationFolderName "Renditions Folder"

## Get-PWRichProjects


NAME
    Get-PWRichProjects
    
SYNOPSIS
    Get-PWRichProjects returns ProjectWise Folder Objects for all of the Work Areas/Rich Projects within current datasource or the specified folder path or matching the type and sample property values.
    
    
SYNTAX
    Get-PWRichProjects [[-FolderPath] <string>] [[-ProjectTypeName] <string>] [[-PopulateProjectProperties] <SwitchParameter>] [[-JustOne] <SwitchParameter>] [[-ProjectProperties] <Hashtable>] [[-PopulatePaths] <SwitchParameter>] [[-FolderName] <string>] [[-BypassSearchAssembly] 
    <SwitchParameter>] [[-OnlyConnectedProjects] <SwitchParameter>] [[-OnlyNonConnectedProjects] <SwitchParameter>] [<CommonParameters>]
    
    
DESCRIPTION
    Get-PWRichProjects returns all of the Work Areas/Rich Projects within current datasource or the specified folder path.
    

PARAMETERS
    -FolderPath <string>
        Search for Rich Projects in this tree.
        
        Required?                    false
        Position?                    0
        Default value                
        Accept pipeline input?       false
        Accept wildcard characters?  false
        
    -ProjectTypeName <string>
        Project Type Name to search for (Required to do Properties Search).
        
        Required?                    false
        Position?                    1
        Default value                
        Accept pipeline input?       false
        Accept wildcard characters?  false
        
    -PopulateProjectProperties <SwitchParameter>
        Set to get Project Properties on folder object populated.
        
        Required?                    false
        Position?                    2
        Default value                False
        Accept pipeline input?       false
        Accept wildcard characters?  false
        
    -JustOne <SwitchParameter>
        Just return project specified by path.
        
        Required?                    false
        Position?                    3
        Default value                False
        Accept pipeline input?       false
        Accept wildcard characters?  false
        
    -ProjectProperties <Hashtable>
        List of project property values to search for (e.g. @{PROJECT_Project_Name='A Project Name'; PROJECT_Project_Number='YYYYY'}. Property names are case sensitive. % supported as wild card on strings.
        
        Required?                    false
        Position?                    4
        Default value                System.Collections.Hashtable
        Accept pipeline input?       false
        Accept wildcard characters?  false
        
    -FolderName <string>
        OBSOLETE. Ignored.
        
        Required?                    false
        Position?                    6
        Default value                
        Accept pipeline input?       false
        Accept wildcard characters?  false
        
    -BypassSearchAssembly <SwitchParameter>
        OBSOLETE. Ignored.
        
        Required?                    false
        Position?                    7
        Default value                False
        Accept pipeline input?       false
        Accept wildcard characters?  false
        
    -PopulatePaths <SwitchParameter>
        Fill in the folder paths.
        
        Required?                    false
        Position?                    5
        Default value                False
        Accept pipeline input?       false
        Accept wildcard characters?  false
        
    -OnlyConnectedProjects <SwitchParameter>
        Set to return only connected projects.
        
        Required?                    false
        Position?                    8
        Default value                False
        Accept pipeline input?       false
        Accept wildcard characters?  false
        
    -OnlyNonConnectedProjects <SwitchParameter>
        Set to return only the projects that are not connected projects.
        
        Required?                    false
        Position?                    9
        Default value                False
        Accept pipeline input?       false
        Accept wildcard characters?  false
        
    <CommonParameters>
        This cmdlet supports the common parameters: Verbose, Debug,
        ErrorAction, ErrorVariable, WarningAction, WarningVariable,
        OutBuffer, PipelineVariable, and OutVariable. For more information, see 
        about_CommonParameters (https:/go.microsoft.com/fwlink/?LinkID=113216). 
    
INPUTS
    
OUTPUTS
    
    ----------  EXAMPLE 1  ----------
    
    #Example usage returning Work Areas/Rich Projects.
    The following will return all Work Areas/Rich Projects within the current ProjectWise Datasource.
    Get-PWRichProjects -Verbose
    
    ----------  EXAMPLE 2  ----------
    
    #The following will return all Work Areas/Rich Projects within the folder path
    $rps = Get-PWRichProjects -FolderPath 'BSI900 - Adelaide Tower' -PopulatePaths
    #The following will return all Work Areas/Rich Projects within the folder path of the given Project Type and will populate the project properties in the returned object.
    $rps1 = Get-PWRichProjects -FolderPath 'Test Rich Connected Projects' -ProjectTypeName 'AllColumnTypes' -PopulateProjectProperties
    #The following will return all Work Areas/Rich Projects of the given Project Type matching the given property values. Property names are case-sensitive.
    $rps2 = Get-PWRichProjects -ProjectTypeName 'AllColumnTypes' -ProjectProperties @{PROJECT_P_STRING = "Some new string"; PROJECT_P_LONGINTEGER = 555} -PopulateProjectProperties
    #The following will return all Work Areas/Rich Projects of the given Project Type and populate the project properties on the returned objects.
    $rps3 = Get-PWRichProjects -ProjectTypeName 'General' -PopulateProjectProperties

## Get-PWSavedSearches


NAME
    Get-PWSavedSearches
    
SYNOPSIS
    Get a list of all saved searches within the current datasource.
    
    
SYNTAX
    Get-PWSavedSearches [[-InputFolder] <ProjectWiseFolder[]>] [[-Personal] <SwitchParameter>] [<CommonParameters>]
    
    Get-PWSavedSearches [[-FolderPath] <string>] [[-Personal] <SwitchParameter>] [<CommonParameters>]
    
    
DESCRIPTION
    Defaults to global saved searches, but user can specify a folder path, an array of folders or whether to return the current user's personal searches.
    

PARAMETERS
    -InputFolder <ProjectWiseFolder[]>
        ProjectWise Folder (Work Area) object(s) to search for saved searches.
        
        Required?                    false
        Position?                    0
        Default value                PWPS_DAB.CommonTypes+ProjectWiseFolder[]
        Accept pipeline input?       true (ByValue)
        Accept wildcard characters?  false
        
    -FolderPath <string>
        Folder path to Work Area to search for saved searches.
        
        Required?                    false
        Position?                    0
        Default value                
        Accept pipeline input?       false
        Accept wildcard characters?  false
        
    -Personal <SwitchParameter>
        Set this to return the current user's personal searches, otherwise global searches will be returned for the datasource or for the project if one is defined.
        
        Required?                    false
        Position?                    1
        Default value                False
        Accept pipeline input?       false
        Accept wildcard characters?  false
        
    <CommonParameters>
        This cmdlet supports the common parameters: Verbose, Debug,
        ErrorAction, ErrorVariable, WarningAction, WarningVariable,
        OutBuffer, PipelineVariable, and OutVariable. For more information, see 
        about_CommonParameters (https:/go.microsoft.com/fwlink/?LinkID=113216). 
    
INPUTS
    PWPS_DAB.CommonTypes+ProjectWiseFolder[]
        ProjectWise Folder (Work Area) object(s) to search for saved searches.
    
    
OUTPUTS
    
    ----------  EXAMPLE 1  ----------
    
    #Example usage getting list of global saved searches within the current datasource.
    #Get the global saved searches within the current datasource.
    Get-PWSavedSearches
    #Get the global saved searches within the given folder.
    Get-PWSavedSearches -FolderPath 'Top Leve\Sub Level\Sub Level2'
    #Get the current user's saved searches within the given folder.
    Get-PWSavedSearches -FolderPath 'Top Leve\Sub Level\Sub Level2' -Personal
    #Get the current user's saved searches at the top level of the datasource.
    Get-PWSavedSearches -Personal
    #Get the current user's saved searches for all the projects in the given path.
    Get-PWRichProjects -FolderPath 'Top Level\Projects' | Get-PWSavedSearches -Personal
    
    
RELATED LINKS

## Get-PWStorageAreaReport


NAME
    Get-PWStorageAreaReport
    
SYNOPSIS
    
    
SYNTAX
    Get-PWStorageAreaReport [[-FolderPath] <string>] [[-StorageAreaName] <string>] [-OutputFolder] <string> [[-UseAdminPaths] <SwitchParameter>] [[-SQLite] <SwitchParameter>] [-SkipFileSizeCheck <SwitchParameter>] [-SkipOrphanedFileCheck <SwitchParameter>] [<CommonParameters>]
    
    
DESCRIPTION
    

PARAMETERS
    -FolderPath <string>
        Folder path of ProjectWise folder to report on.
        
        Required?                    false
        Position?                    0
        Default value                
        Accept pipeline input?       true (ByValue)
        Accept wildcard characters?  false
        
    -StorageAreaName <string>
        Name of storage area to report on.
        
        Required?                    false
        Position?                    0
        Default value                
        Accept pipeline input?       true (ByValue)
        Accept wildcard characters?  false
        
    -OutputFolder <string>
        Folder path to create output file in.
        
        Required?                    true
        Position?                    1
        Default value                
        Accept pipeline input?       true (ByValue)
        Accept wildcard characters?  false
        
    -UseAdminPaths <SwitchParameter>
        When UseAdminPaths is included, administrative paths to the files will be used.".
        
        Required?                    false
        Position?                    2
        Default value                False
        Accept pipeline input?       false
        Accept wildcard characters?  false
        
    -SQLite <SwitchParameter>
        Output SQLite rather than XLSX.
        
        Required?                    false
        Position?                    3
        Default value                False
        Accept pipeline input?       false
        Accept wildcard characters?  false
        
    -SkipFileSizeCheck <SwitchParameter>
        When included, skips the file size check.
        
        Required?                    false
        Position?                    named
        Default value                False
        Accept pipeline input?       false
        Accept wildcard characters?  false
        
    -SkipOrphanedFileCheck <SwitchParameter>
        When included, skips the check for orphaned files.
        
        Required?                    false
        Position?                    named
        Default value                False
        Accept pipeline input?       false
        Accept wildcard characters?  false
        
    <CommonParameters>
        This cmdlet supports the common parameters: Verbose, Debug,
        ErrorAction, ErrorVariable, WarningAction, WarningVariable,
        OutBuffer, PipelineVariable, and OutVariable. For more information, see 
        about_CommonParameters (https:/go.microsoft.com/fwlink/?LinkID=113216). 
    
INPUTS
    System.String
        Folder path of ProjectWise folder to report on.
    
    System.String
        Name of storage area to report on.
    
    System.String
        Folder path to create output file in.
    
    
OUTPUTS
    
    ----------  EXAMPLE 1  ----------
    
    The following will create a storage area report for an entire datasource.
    Get-PWStorageAreaReport -OutputFolder 'D:\Reports' -Verbose
    
    ----------  EXAMPLE 2  ----------
    
    The following will create a storage area report for a specified project.
    Get-PWStorageAreaReport -FolderPath 'Projects\MyProject' -OutputFolder 'D:\Reports' -Verbose
    
    ----------  EXAMPLE 3  ----------
    
    The following will create a storage area report for a specified storage area.
    Get-PWStorageAreaReport -StorageAreaName 'Storage_01' -OutputFolder 'D:\Reports' -Verbose
    
    ----------  EXAMPLE 4  ----------
    
    The following will create a storage area report for an entire datasource. Skipping the file size check.
    Get-PWStorageAreaReport -OutputFolder 'D:\Reports' -SkipFileSizeCheck -Verbose
    
    ----------  EXAMPLE 5  ----------
    
    The following will create a storage area report for an entire datasource. Skipping the orphaned file check.
    Get-PWStorageAreaReport -OutputFolder 'D:\Reports' -SkipOrphanCheck -Verbose
    
    ----------  EXAMPLE 6  ----------
    
    The UseAdminPaths will use UNC paths rather than literal.  Example: '\\BMF-WS2016\C$\ProjectWise\StorageAreas\BMF_PW\Storage_01'
    The following will create a storage area report for an entire datasource. Using admin paths and skipping the orphaned file check.
    Get-PWStorageAreaReport -OutputFolder 'D:\Reports' -SkipOrphanCheck -UseAdminPaths -Verbose
    
    
RELATED LINKS

## Get-PWUserByLastLogin


NAME
    Get-PWUserByLastLogin
    
SYNOPSIS
    Get users by the user's last login.
    
    
SYNTAX
    Get-PWUserByLastLogin [[-DaysAgo] <int>] [[-Since] <SwitchParameter>] [[-IdentityInfo] <SwitchParameter>] [<CommonParameters>]
    
    
DESCRIPTION
    Get users by their last login. Requires admin pripileges.
    

PARAMETERS
    -DaysAgo <int>
        Defines the login window in days to use.
        
        Required?                    false
        Position?                    0
        Default value                0
        Accept pipeline input?       false
        Accept wildcard characters?  false
        
    -Since <SwitchParameter>
        Use this to get the logins within the window. Without this switch, will default to listing users with last logins outside the window (older) and users who have never logged in.
        
        Required?                    false
        Position?                    1
        Default value                False
        Accept pipeline input?       false
        Accept wildcard characters?  false
        
    -IdentityInfo <SwitchParameter>
        Use this parameter to get the identity and identity provider. Its use has the potential to slow the cmdlet down significantly. Its use requires the currently logged in user to have admin privileges.
        
        Required?                    false
        Position?                    2
        Default value                False
        Accept pipeline input?       false
        Accept wildcard characters?  false
        
    <CommonParameters>
        This cmdlet supports the common parameters: Verbose, Debug,
        ErrorAction, ErrorVariable, WarningAction, WarningVariable,
        OutBuffer, PipelineVariable, and OutVariable. For more information, see 
        about_CommonParameters (https:/go.microsoft.com/fwlink/?LinkID=113216). 
    
INPUTS
    
OUTPUTS
    
    ----------  EXAMPLE 1  ----------
    
    Report on all users and when they last logged in:
    
    Get-PWUserByLastLogin
    
    ----------  EXAMPLE 2  ----------
    
    Report on users that last logged in from 30 days ago until logins were first tracked:
    
    Get-PWUserByLastLogin -DaysAgo 30
    
    ----------  EXAMPLE 3  ----------
    
    Report on users that last logged in from 30 days ago until the present:
    
    Get-PWUserByLastLogin -DaysAgo 30 -Since

## Get-PWWorkAreaConnections


NAME
    Get-PWWorkAreaConnections
    
SYNOPSIS
    Gets Work Area Connections from the connected projects associated with these folders.
    
    
SYNTAX
    Get-PWWorkAreaConnections [[-InputFolder] <ProjectWiseFolder[]>] [-Token] <string> [[-WSGVersion] <string>] [[-ConnectedProjectIds] <string[]>] [<CommonParameters>]
    
    
DESCRIPTION
    Takes an array of ProjectWiseFolders and returns work area connection objects.
    

PARAMETERS
    -InputFolder <ProjectWiseFolder[]>
        Array of ProjectWise folders from pipeline.
        
        Required?                    false
        Position?                    0
        Default value                PWPS_DAB.CommonTypes+ProjectWiseFolder[]
        Accept pipeline input?       true (ByValue)
        Accept wildcard characters?  false
        
    -Token <string>
        Pass base 64 encoded token from Get-PWConnectionClientToken or from Get-PWNonFederatedLoginToken -CreateWebToken.
        
        Required?                    true
        Position?                    1
        Default value                
        Accept pipeline input?       false
        Accept wildcard characters?  false
        
    -WSGVersion <string>
        WSG Version. Defaults to v2.5.
        
        Required?                    false
        Position?                    2
        Default value                v2.5
        Accept pipeline input?       false
        Accept wildcard characters?  false
        
    -ConnectedProjectIds <string[]>
        List of Connected Project Ids.
        
        Required?                    false
        Position?                    3
        Default value                System.String[]
        Accept pipeline input?       false
        Accept wildcard characters?  false
        
    <CommonParameters>
        This cmdlet supports the common parameters: Verbose, Debug,
        ErrorAction, ErrorVariable, WarningAction, WarningVariable,
        OutBuffer, PipelineVariable, and OutVariable. For more information, see 
        about_CommonParameters (https:/go.microsoft.com/fwlink/?LinkID=113216). 
    
INPUTS
    PWPS_DAB.CommonTypes+ProjectWiseFolder[]
        Array of ProjectWise folders from pipeline.
    
    
OUTPUTS
    System.Collections.Generic.List`1[[PWPS_DAB.ConnectedProjectAdapter+WorkAreaConnection, PWPS_DAB, Version=24.0.2.0, Culture=neutral, PublicKeyToken=null]]
    
    
    ----------  EXAMPLE 1  ----------
    
    #Example usage for getting the Work Area Connections for each rich project in a tree.
    $rps = Get-PWRichProjects -OnlyConnectedProjects
    #foreach Connected Project, get the Work Area Connections
    $token = Get-PWConnectionClientToken
    foreach ($rp in $rps) 
    {
    write-host $rp
    Get-PWWorkAreaConnections $rp -Token $token 
    }
    
    
RELATED LINKS

        Required?                    true
        Position?                    1
        Default value                
        Accept pipeline input?       false
        Accept wildcard characters?  false

        Required?                    true

        Default value

## Import-PWEnvironments


NAME
    Import-PWEnvironments
    
SYNOPSIS
    Import and update environments from a spreadsheet generated by Export-PWEnvironments.
    
    
SYNTAX
    Import-PWEnvironments [-InputFileName] <string> [[-Environments] <string[]>] [[-Interfaces] <string[]>] [[-ApplyDocumentCodeDefinition] <SwitchParameter>] [<CommonParameters>]
    
    
DESCRIPTION
    This is intended to be a smarter and more flexible alternative to using AAM files to maintain environments.
    
    Column type keywords supported are text, int, numeric and datetime.
    
    You can update existing environments such as adding attributes by adding lines to the spreadsheet. You can change properties for existing attributes by changing the appropriate columns in the spreadsheet. Triggers, defaults and lookups can be added, modified or removed. Triggering 
    columns can be easily changed. Edit control types, format strings, etc. can all be changed.
    
    Interfaces can be added or replaced by changing the Interfaces tab. Interface elements can be added or moved or changed.
    
    Document code definitions can be modified or removed. Use the -ApplyDocumentCodeDefintion switch.
    
    Adding columns works well with SQL Server and Oracle. If table creation on new environment fails in either SQL Server or Oracle, this probably has to do with a reserved word being used, an invalid column name or an invalid width for a column. Debug by taking the displayed DDL for 
    the new table and executing it in SQL Plus (change the table name). Oracle should tell you the issue in an interactive session as will SQL Server Management Studio. Then, just update the spreadsheet and try again.
    

PARAMETERS
    -InputFileName <string>
        Input file name. Should be file in the format generated by Export-PWEnvironments
        
        Required?                    true
        Position?                    0
        Default value                
        Accept pipeline input?       false
        Accept wildcard characters?  false
        
    -Environments <string[]>
        Provide environment names to limit import. Otherwise, imports all environments in spreadsheet.
        
        Required?                    false
        Position?                    2
        Default value                
        Accept pipeline input?       false
        Accept wildcard characters?  false
        
    -Interfaces <string[]>
        Provide Interface names to limit import. Otherwise, imports all interface definitions in spreadsheet.
        
        Required?                    false
        Position?                    3
        Default value                
        Accept pipeline input?       false
        Accept wildcard characters?  false
        
    -ApplyDocumentCodeDefinition <SwitchParameter>
        Set this switch to replace an existing document code definition (use with caution).
        
        Required?                    false
        Position?                    4
        Default value                False
        Accept pipeline input?       false
        Accept wildcard characters?  false
        
    <CommonParameters>
        This cmdlet supports the common parameters: Verbose, Debug,
        ErrorAction, ErrorVariable, WarningAction, WarningVariable,
        OutBuffer, PipelineVariable, and OutVariable. For more information, see 
        about_CommonParameters (https:/go.microsoft.com/fwlink/?LinkID=113216). 
    
INPUTS
    
OUTPUTS
    
    ----------  EXAMPLE 1  ----------
    
    Import-PWEnvironments c:\report\environments.xlsx -Environments Simple,Complex
    
    
RELATED LINKS

    #Get all the folders in this tree
    $folders = Get-PWFoldersHashTableByID -FolderPath "PWPS Connected Project Test 6\Projects 2"
    Save-PWFoldersHashTable $folders -OutputFileName c:\temp\FoldersByID.sqlite
    $folders2 = Import-PWFoldersHashTable c:\temp\FoldersByID.sqlite

## Import-PWLookupTableFromDataTable


NAME
    Import-PWLookupTableFromDataTable
    
SYNOPSIS
    Write the values from a datatable into a table in the PW database for lookup table maintenance.
    
    
SYNTAX
    Import-PWLookupTableFromDataTable [-InputTable] <DataTable> [-TableName] <string> [[-Append] <SwitchParameter>] [[-DropFirst] <SwitchParameter>] [<CommonParameters>]
    
    
DESCRIPTION
    

PARAMETERS
    -InputTable <DataTable>
        Data Table object to import (Required).
        
        Required?                    true
        Position?                    0
        Default value                
        Accept pipeline input?       true (ByValue)
        Accept wildcard characters?  false
        
    -TableName <string>
        Table name to insert values into (Required).
        
        Required?                    true
        Position?                    1
        Default value                
        Accept pipeline input?       false
        Accept wildcard characters?  false
        
    -Append <SwitchParameter>
        Set this to preserve existing rows.
        
        Required?                    false
        Position?                    2
        Default value                False
        Accept pipeline input?       false
        Accept wildcard characters?  false
        
    -DropFirst <SwitchParameter>
        Set this to preserve existing rows.
        
        Required?                    false
        Position?                    3
        Default value                False
        Accept pipeline input?       false
        Accept wildcard characters?  false
        
    <CommonParameters>
        This cmdlet supports the common parameters: Verbose, Debug,
        ErrorAction, ErrorVariable, WarningAction, WarningVariable,
        OutBuffer, PipelineVariable, and OutVariable. For more information, see 
        about_CommonParameters (https:/go.microsoft.com/fwlink/?LinkID=113216). 
    
INPUTS
    System.Data.DataTable
        Data Table object to import (Required).
    
    
OUTPUTS
    
    ----------  EXAMPLE 1  ----------
    
    $connectionString="DSN=OracleInstant;Pwd=pass"
    $query="select * from v_filepurpose"
    $conn = New-Object System.Data.Odbc.OdbcConnection
    $conn.ConnectionString = $connectionString
    $conn.open()
    $cmd = New-object System.Data.Odbc.OdbcCommand($query,$conn)
    $ds = New-Object system.Data.DataSet
    (New-Object system.Data.odbc.odbcDataAdapter($cmd)).fill($ds) | out-null
    $conn.close()
    Import-PWLookupTableFromDataTable $ds.Tables[0] -TableName MyLookupTable -DropFirst

## Import-PWProjectAccessControl


NAME
    Import-PWProjectAccessControl
    
SYNOPSIS
    Import-PWProjectAccessControl will update project access control based on the access control settings imported from the specified datatable, Excel spreadsheet or SQLite database.
    
    
SYNTAX
    Import-PWProjectAccessControl [[-InputFolder] <ProjectWiseFolder>] [-ImportFilePathName] <string> [<CommonParameters>]
    
    Import-PWProjectAccessControl [[-InputFolder] <ProjectWiseFolder>] [-ImportDatatable] <DataTable> [<CommonParameters>]
    
    
DESCRIPTION
    Use to update a projects access control settings in its entirety. Or import the access control data into a datatable. Use the Export-PWProjectAccessControl to export the access control to a datatable, spreadsheet or SQLite database.
    

PARAMETERS
    -InputFolder <ProjectWiseFolder>
        Target folder object from pipeline. If excluded, a datatable will be returned.
        
        Required?                    false
        Position?                    0
        Default value                
        Accept pipeline input?       true (ByValue)
        Accept wildcard characters?  false
        
    -ImportFilePathName <string>
        
        Required?                    true
        Position?                    1
        Default value                
        Accept pipeline input?       false
        Accept wildcard characters?  false
        
    -ImportDatatable <DataTable>
        
        Required?                    true
        Position?                    1
        Default value                
        Accept pipeline input?       false
        Accept wildcard characters?  false
        
    <CommonParameters>
        This cmdlet supports the common parameters: Verbose, Debug,
        ErrorAction, ErrorVariable, WarningAction, WarningVariable,
        OutBuffer, PipelineVariable, and OutVariable. For more information, see 
        about_CommonParameters (https:/go.microsoft.com/fwlink/?LinkID=113216). 
    
INPUTS
    PWPS_DAB.CommonTypes+ProjectWiseFolder
        Target folder object from pipeline. If excluded, a datatable will be returned.
    
    
OUTPUTS
    
    ----------  EXAMPLE 1  ----------
    
    Updates the access control for the specified project, based on the information imported in from the spreadsheet.
    Get-PWFolders -FolderID 69989 -JustOne | Import-PWProjectAccessControl -ImportFilePathName d:\temp\import\projectaccesscontrol.xlsx
    
    ----------  EXAMPLE 2  ----------
    
    Updates the access control for the specified project, based on the information imported in from the SQLite database.
    $pwFolders = Get-PWFolders -FolderID 69989 -JustOne;  Import-PWProjectAccessControl -InputFolder $pwFolder -ImportFilePathName d:\temp\import\projectaccesscontrol.xlsx
    
    ----------  EXAMPLE 3  ----------
    
    Updates the access control for the specified project, based on the information imported in from the datatable.
     
    $dt = Export-PWProjectAccessControl -InputFolder (Get-PWFolders -FolderID 70383 -JustOne) -Verbose
    Import-PWProjectAccessControl -InputFolder $pwFolder -ImportDatatable $dt -Verbose
    
    
RELATED LINKS

## Move-PWDocumentsToFolder


NAME
    Move-PWDocumentsToFolder
    
SYNOPSIS
    Moves documents to a target folder.
    
    
SYNTAX
    Move-PWDocumentsToFolder [-InputDocument] <ProjectWiseDocument[]> [-TargetFolderPath] <string> [[-CreateVersion] <SwitchParameter>] [[-DoNotPreserveState] <SwitchParameter>] [[-PreserveSourceState] <SwitchParameter>] [<CommonParameters>]
    
    
DESCRIPTION
    Takes an array of document objects from the pipeline and moves them to a target folder.
    

PARAMETERS
    -InputDocument <ProjectWiseDocument[]>
        Array of document objects from pipeline (Required).
        
        Required?                    true
        Position?                    0
        Default value                
        Accept pipeline input?       true (ByValue)
        Accept wildcard characters?  false
        
    -TargetFolderPath <string>
        Path to target folder (Required).
        
        Required?                    true
        Position?                    1
        Default value                
        Accept pipeline input?       false
        Accept wildcard characters?  false
        
    -CreateVersion <SwitchParameter>
        Set this to create a new version if the document exists. If not set, document will be skipped.
        
        Required?                    false
        Position?                    2
        Default value                False
        Accept pipeline input?       false
        Accept wildcard characters?  false
        
    -DoNotPreserveState <SwitchParameter>
        Set this to bypass workflow state preservation.
        
        Required?                    false
        Position?                    3
        Default value                False
        Accept pipeline input?       false
        Accept wildcard characters?  false
        
    -PreserveSourceState <SwitchParameter>
        (Obsolete) argument is ignored. Preserved for backward compatibility.
        
        Required?                    false
        Position?                    4
        Default value                False
        Accept pipeline input?       false
        Accept wildcard characters?  false
        
    <CommonParameters>
        This cmdlet supports the common parameters: Verbose, Debug,
        ErrorAction, ErrorVariable, WarningAction, WarningVariable,
        OutBuffer, PipelineVariable, and OutVariable. For more information, see 
        about_CommonParameters (https:/go.microsoft.com/fwlink/?LinkID=113216). 
    
INPUTS
    PWPS_DAB.CommonTypes+ProjectWiseDocument[]
        Array of document objects from pipeline (Required).
    
    
OUTPUTS
    
    ----------  EXAMPLE 1  ----------
    
    # Get the documents in the given path and move them to a target folder. Document states will be preserved in the target folder.
    Get-PWDocumentsBySearch -FolderPath 'Import\Test' -FileName '02_%.pdf'| Move-PWDocumentsToFolder -TargetFolderPath 'New\Folder\Path'
    
    ----------  EXAMPLE 2  ----------
    
    # Get the documents in the folder and move them to a target folder. Do not preserve the source state for each document.
    $pwDocs = Get-PWDocumentsBySearch -FolderID 70383 -JustThisFolder
                $pwDocsMoved = Move-PWDocumentsToFolder -InputDocument $pwDocs -TargetFolderPath 'PowerShell\PowerShell_Target' -DoNotPreserveState -Verbose
    
    ----------  EXAMPLE 3  ----------
    
    # Get the documents in the folder and move them to a target folder. Create versions if documents exist in target. Document states will be preserved in the target folder. Except for any new document versions.
    $pwDocs = Get-PWDocumentsBySearch -FolderID 70383 -JustThisFolder
                $pwDocsMoved = Move-PWDocumentsToFolder -InputDocument $pwDocs -TargetFolderPath 'PowerShell\PowerShell_Target' -CreateVersion -Verbose
    
    ----------  EXAMPLE 4  ----------
    
    # Get the documents in the folder and move them to a target folder. Create versions if documents exist in target. Document states will be preserved in the target folder, including new document versions.
    $pwDocs = Get-PWDocumentsBySearch -FolderID 70383 -JustThisFolder
                $pwDocsMoved = Move-PWDocumentsToFolder -InputDocument $pwDocs -TargetFolderPath 'PowerShell\PowerShell_Target' -CreateVersion -PreserveSourceState -Verbose
    
    
RELATED LINKS

## Move-PWLogInOutAuditTrailRecords


NAME
    Move-PWLogInOutAuditTrailRecords
    
SYNOPSIS
    Moves user login/logout audit trail entries from the primary audit trail table to the secondary.
    
    
SYNTAX
    Move-PWLogInOutAuditTrailRecords [[-StartDate] <string>] [[-EndDate] <string>] [<CommonParameters>]
    
    
DESCRIPTION
    

PARAMETERS
    -StartDate <string>
        
        Required?                    false
        Position?                    0
        Default value                
        Accept pipeline input?       false
        Accept wildcard characters?  false
        
    -EndDate <string>
        
        Required?                    false
        Position?                    1
        Default value                
        Accept pipeline input?       false
        Accept wildcard characters?  false
        
    <CommonParameters>
        This cmdlet supports the common parameters: Verbose, Debug,
        ErrorAction, ErrorVariable, WarningAction, WarningVariable,
        OutBuffer, PipelineVariable, and OutVariable. For more information, see 
        about_CommonParameters (https:/go.microsoft.com/fwlink/?LinkID=113216). 
    
INPUTS
    
OUTPUTS
    
    ----------  EXAMPLE 1  ----------
    
    Moves all user login/logout records to the secondary audit trail table.
    Move-PWLogInOutAuditTrailRecords -Verbose
    
    ----------  EXAMPLE 2  ----------
    
    Moves all user login/logout records between the two provided dates to the secondary audit trail table.
    Move-PWLogInOutAuditTrailRecords -StartDate 04/01/2018 -EndDate 04/05/2018 -Verbose
    
    ----------  EXAMPLE 3  ----------
    
    Moves all user login/logout records between the start date provided and the current date to the secondary audit trail table.
    Move-PWLogInOutAuditTrailRecords -StartDate 04/01/2018 -Verbose

## New-PWDocument


NAME
    New-PWDocument
    
SYNOPSIS
    Given a folder object or folder path and path to an existing file create a new document without attributes.
    
    
SYNTAX
    New-PWDocument [[-InputFolders] <ProjectWiseFolder[]>] [-FilePath] <string> [[-Description] <string>] [[-Version] <string>] [[-Application] <string>] [[-DocumentName] <string>] [<CommonParameters>]
    
    New-PWDocument [[-FolderPath] <string>] [-FilePath] <string> [[-Description] <string>] [[-Version] <string>] [[-Application] <string>] [[-DocumentName] <string>] [<CommonParameters>]
    
    
DESCRIPTION
    

PARAMETERS
    -InputFolders <ProjectWiseFolder[]>
        Target folder object(s) from pipeline.
        
        Required?                    false
        Position?                    0
        Default value                PWPS_DAB.CommonTypes+ProjectWiseFolder[]
        Accept pipeline input?       true (ByValue)
        Accept wildcard characters?  false
        
    -FolderPath <string>
        Target folder path (not required if sending folder(s) on pipeline.
        
        Required?                    false
        Position?                    1
        Default value                
        Accept pipeline input?       false
        Accept wildcard characters?  false
        
    -FilePath <string>
        Path to file on disk.
        
        Required?                    true
        Position?                    2
        Default value                
        Accept pipeline input?       false
        Accept wildcard characters?  false
        
    -Description <string>
        Description of new document (optional).
        
        Required?                    false
        Position?                    3
        Default value                
        Accept pipeline input?       false
        Accept wildcard characters?  false
        
    -Version <string>
        Version string for new document (optional).
        
        Required?                    false
        Position?                    4
        Default value                
        Accept pipeline input?       false
        Accept wildcard characters?  false
        
    -Application <string>
        Application Name to use (optional). Will use default application for file extension if not supplied.
        
        Required?                    false
        Position?                    5
        Default value                
        Accept pipeline input?       false
        Accept wildcard characters?  false
        
    -DocumentName <string>
        Document Name to use. FileName used if not supplied.
        
        Required?                    false
        Position?                    6
        Default value                
        Accept pipeline input?       false
        Accept wildcard characters?  false
        
    <CommonParameters>
        This cmdlet supports the common parameters: Verbose, Debug,
        ErrorAction, ErrorVariable, WarningAction, WarningVariable,
        OutBuffer, PipelineVariable, and OutVariable. For more information, see 
        about_CommonParameters (https:/go.microsoft.com/fwlink/?LinkID=113216). 
    
INPUTS
    PWPS_DAB.CommonTypes+ProjectWiseFolder[]
        Target folder object(s) from pipeline.
    
    
OUTPUTS
    
    ----------  EXAMPLE 1  ----------
    
    #Example usage getting folders and creating new documents.
    New-PWLogin Server:DSN
    #Get the folder for folder number 20315 and create a new document there
    Get-PWFolders 20315 | New-PWDocument -FilePath c:\temp\NewDrawing.dgn
    #Get the folder at the given folder path and create a document there
    Get-PWFolders -FolderPath 'Level 1\Level 2\Level 3\Level 4' -JustOne | New-PWDocument -FilePath c:\temp\NewDrawing.dgn -Description 'Drawing 1'
    #Create a new folder at the given folder path and create a document there
    New-PWFolder -FolderPath 'PowerShell Demo\Level 2\Level 3\Level 4' -StorageArea Storage01 | New-PWDocument -FilePath c:\temp\NewDrawing.dgn -Description 'Drawing 1'
    #Create a new document in existing folder
    New-PWDocument -FolderPath 'Demo\Folder 1' -FilePath c:\temp\NewDrawing.dgn -Description 'Drawing 1'

## New-PWDocumentAbstract


NAME
    New-PWDocumentAbstract
    
SYNOPSIS
    Given a folder object or folder path, create one or more abstract documents without attributes.
    
    
SYNTAX
    New-PWDocumentAbstract [-InputFolders] <ProjectWiseFolder[]> [[-DocumentName] <string>] [[-Description] <string>] [[-Version] <string>] [-Count <int>] [-DoNotAddSuffix <SwitchParameter>] [<CommonParameters>]
    
    New-PWDocumentAbstract [[-DocumentName] <string>] [[-Description] <string>] [[-Version] <string>] -FolderPath <string> [-Count <int>] [-DoNotAddSuffix <SwitchParameter>] [<CommonParameters>]
    
    
DESCRIPTION
    Given a folder object or folder path, create one or more abstract documents without attributes. When the DoNotAddSuffix parameter is included, the 5 digit serial number will not be placed at the end of the document name and only one document will be added to each folder regardless 
    of the count entered.
    

PARAMETERS
    -InputFolders <ProjectWiseFolder[]>
        Target folder object(s) from pipeline.
        
        Required?                    true
        Position?                    0
        Default value                PWPS_DAB.CommonTypes+ProjectWiseFolder[]
        Accept pipeline input?       true (ByValue)
        Accept wildcard characters?  false
        
    -FolderPath <string>
        Target folder path (not required if sending folder(s) on pipeline).
        
        Required?                    true
        Position?                    named
        Default value                
        Accept pipeline input?       false
        Accept wildcard characters?  false
        
    -DocumentName <string>
        Name to prefix abstract document (Optional) If excluded, 'doc' will be used.
        
        Required?                    false
        Position?                    1
        Default value                
        Accept pipeline input?       false
        Accept wildcard characters?  false
        
    -Description <string>
        Description of new document (optional). If excluded, the document name will be used.
        
        Required?                    false
        Position?                    2
        Default value                
        Accept pipeline input?       false
        Accept wildcard characters?  false
        
    -Version <string>
        Version string to use for new document (optional).
        
        Required?                    false
        Position?                    3
        Default value                
        Accept pipeline input?       false
        Accept wildcard characters?  false
        
    -Count <int>
        Number of abstract documents to create. (Optional) If excluded, only one will be created
        
        Required?                    false
        Position?                    named
        Default value                0
        Accept pipeline input?       false
        Accept wildcard characters?  false
        
    -DoNotAddSuffix <SwitchParameter>
        When included, the 5 digit serial number suffix will not be added to the document name and only one document will be added to each folder regardless of the count entered.
        
        Required?                    false
        Position?                    named
        Default value                False
        Accept pipeline input?       false
        Accept wildcard characters?  false
        
    <CommonParameters>
        This cmdlet supports the common parameters: Verbose, Debug,
        ErrorAction, ErrorVariable, WarningAction, WarningVariable,
        OutBuffer, PipelineVariable, and OutVariable. For more information, see 
        about_CommonParameters (https:/go.microsoft.com/fwlink/?LinkID=113216). 
    
INPUTS
    PWPS_DAB.CommonTypes+ProjectWiseFolder[]
        Target folder object(s) from pipeline.
    
    
OUTPUTS
    
    ----------  EXAMPLE 1  ----------
    
    #Example usage getting folders and creating new documents.
    # To create abstract documents without getting InputFolders from the pipeline
        Supply the folder full path using -FolderPath, supply document name (optional), 
        document description (optional) and/or count (optional) and create a new document there
    New-PWDocumentAbstract -FolderPath 'Level 1\' -DocumentName 'doc' -Description 'Abstract Document'
    New-PWDocumentAbstract -FolderPath 'Level 1\' -DocumentName 'AbstractDoc' -Count 2
    
    ----------  EXAMPLE 2  ----------
    
    # To create abstract documents while getting InputFolders from the pipeline, supply document name (optional), 
        document description (optional) and/or count (optional) and create a new document there
    Get-PWFolders -FolderPath 'Level 1\Level 2\Level 3\Level 4' -JustOne | New-PWDocumentAbstract -DocumentName 'doc'
    Get-PWFolders -FolderPath 'Level 1\' | New-PWDocumentAbstract -DocumentName 'AbstractDoc' -Count 3
    
    ----------  EXAMPLE 3  ----------
    
    The following example will create one document within each folder without adding the 5 digit serial number suffix.
    Get-PWFolders -FolderPath 'Level 1' | New-PWDocumentAbstract -DocumentName 'doc' -DoNotAddSuffix
    
    
RELATED LINKS

        Accept wildcard characters?  false

        Position?                    named

        Accept wildcard characters?  false

        SetName = 'MyTest'

      $SetFileInfo = @{
        FolderPath = 'Projects'
        SetName = 'MyTest'
        SetDescription = 'New Set File'
        SetMemberName = '2D-M-SAB-LNWK.dwg'
        SetMemberPath = 'Projects\Upload\Sub-Folder'}
    New-PWDocumentFlatSet @SetFileInfo -CheckOut -VersionLock -Verbose
